title.zh: 卷六十 吳書十五 賀全呂周鍾離傳
title.en: Volume 60: Book of Wu 15 - Biographies of He, Quan, Lü, Zhou, and Zhongli
title.raw: 卷六十 吳書十五 賀全呂周鍾離傳 Volume 60: Book of Wu 15 - Biographies of He, Quan, Lü, Zhou, and Zhongli

sentences.zh: 賀齊字公苗，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: He Qi, courtesy name Gongmiao, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi, whose courtesy name was Gongmiao, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《虞预晋书》曰：贺氏本姓庆氏。

translations.literal: 〈The Jin shu of Yu Yu states: The He clan's original surname was the Qing clan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yu Yu’s Jin shu notes that the He family was originally surnamed Qing.

sentences.zh: 齐伯父纯，儒学有重名，汉安帝时为侍中、江夏太守，去官，与江夏黄琼、

translations.literal: Qi's uncle by the elder line, Chun, had heavy fame in Confucian learning; in the time of Emperor An of Han he was Palace Attendant and Administrator of Jiangxia; leaving office, together with Huang Qiong of Jiangxia
translations.idiomatic: His uncle He Chun was a noted Confucian who served as Palace Attendant and prefect of Jiangxia under Han Emperor An; after retiring he was summoned with Huang Qiong of Jiangxia

sentences.zh: （汉中）

translations.literal: (Hanzhong)
translations.idiomatic: (text reads “Hanzhong,” an editorial gloss)

sentences.zh: 〔广汉〕杨厚俱公车徵。

translations.literal: Yang Hou of Guanghan were both summoned by imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: and Yang Hou of Guanghan—by imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 避安帝父孝德皇

translations.literal: to avoid the taboo on the name of Emperor An's father, the Virtuous Emperor
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the taboo name of Emperor An’s father, the posthumously titled Virtuous Emperor,

translations.literal: (the emperor)
translations.idiomatic: (the gloss marks the taboo referent as “the emperor”)

sentences.zh: 讳，改为贺氏。

translations.literal: they changed the surname to He.
translations.idiomatic: the clan changed its surname to He.

sentences.zh: 齐父辅，永宁长。〉

translations.literal: Qi's father Fu was magistrate of Yongning.〉
translations.idiomatic: He Qi’s father He Fu was magistrate of Yongning.〉

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，守剡長。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk of the commandery and acting magistrate of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commandery clerk and acting magistrate of Shan county.

sentences.zh: 縣吏斯從輕俠為奸，齊欲治之。

translations.literal: The county clerk Si Cong, relying on bravado, acted wickedly; Qi wished to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The county clerk Si Cong swaggered and broke the law; He Qi meant to bring him to justice.

sentences.zh: 主簿諫曰：“從，縣大族，山越所附，今日治之，明日寇至。

translations.literal: The chief clerk remonstrated, saying, "Cong is a great clan of the county; the mountain Yue attach to him—if you punish him today, raiders will come tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk warned him: “Si Cong heads a powerful lineage the hill Yue rally to—move against him today and bandits will be at the walls tomorrow.”

sentences.zh: ”齊聞大怒，便立斬眾。

translations.literal: " Qi, hearing this, was greatly angry and at once had Cong executed in public.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi flew into a rage and had Si Cong executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 從族黨遂相糾合，眾千餘人，舉兵攻縣。

translations.literal: Cong's lineage and faction thereupon gathered in mutual alliance, more than a thousand men, and raised arms to attack the county.
translations.idiomatic: Si Cong’s kinsmen mustered over a thousand fighters and stormed the county seat.

sentences.zh: 齊率吏民，開城門突擊，大破之，威震山越。

translations.literal: Qi led clerks and commoners, opened the city gate, and struck in a sudden attack, greatly defeating them; his might shook the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi led militia out the gates in a sally and shattered them, and his name terrified the hill Yue.

sentences.zh: 後太末、豐浦民反，轉守太末長，誅惡養善，期用盡平。

translations.literal: Later the people of Taimo and Fengpu rebelled; he was transferred to defend as magistrate of Taimo, executed the wicked and nurtured the good, and within the allotted period used it all up in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When Taimo and Fengpu rose, he was shifted to Taimo as magistrate, executed ringleaders, shielded the innocent, and pacified the district within his term.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，孫策臨郡，察齊孝廉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an, when Sun Ce came to the commandery, he examined Qi as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 1 Sun Ce took Kuaiji and nominated He Qi as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 時王朗奔東冶，侯官長商升為朗起兵。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Lang fled to Dongye; the magistrate of Houguan, Shang Sheng, raised troops for Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang had fled to Dongye; Shang Sheng, magistrate of Houguan, mustered troops for him.

sentences.zh: 策遣永寧長韓晏領南部都尉，將兵討升，以齊為永寧長。

translations.literal: Ce dispatched the magistrate of Yongning, Han Yan, to lead the Commandant of the Southern Section and campaign against Sheng, with Qi as magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent Han Yan of Yongning south as area commandant against Shang Sheng and named He Qi magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 晏為升所敗，齊又代晏領都尉事。

translations.literal: Yan was defeated by Sheng; Qi again replaced Yan in charge of the commandant's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yan lost to Shang Sheng; He Qi then took his place as southern commandant.

sentences.zh: 升畏齊威名，遣使乞盟。

translations.literal: Sheng feared Qi's dread name and sent an envoy begging alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Sheng, awed by He Qi’s reputation, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 齊因告喻，為陳禍福，升遂送上印綬，出捨求降。

translations.literal: Qi accordingly sent admonitions, setting forth fortune and disaster for him, and Sheng thereupon sent up his seal and ribbon, left his quarters, and sought to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi parleyed, sketching survival and ruin, until Shang Sheng handed over his seal, left his camp, and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 賊帥張雅、詹強等不願升降，反共殺升，雅稱無上將軍，強稱會稽太守。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Zhang Ya, Zhan Qiang, and others were unwilling to follow Sheng in surrender; they turned together and killed Sheng; Ya styled himself General Without Superior, Qiang styled himself Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit leaders Zhang Ya and Zhan Qiang refused to submit with Shang Sheng, murdered him, and Zhang Ya declared himself “general without superior” while Zhan Qiang called himself prefect of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 賊盛兵少，未足以討，齊住軍息兵。

translations.literal: The bandits were strong and the troops few, not enough to campaign; Qi halted the army and rested the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outnumbered him, so He Qi held his troops and waited.

sentences.zh: 雅與女婿何雄爭勢兩乖，齊令越人因事交構。

translations.literal: Ya and his son-in-law He Xiong contended for power and the two fell out; Qi ordered Yue people to stir strife between them on opportune occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ya feuded with his son-in-law He Xiong; He Qi had Yue agents widen the crack.

sentences.zh: 遂至疑隙，阻兵相圖。

translations.literal: They reached mutual suspicion and rift, blocked one another with arms, and plotted against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion hardened until they pointed spears at each other.

sentences.zh: 齊乃進討，一戰大破雅，強黨震懼，率眾出降。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon advanced to punish them; in one battle he greatly broke Ya; Qiang's faction trembled in fear and led the host to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi then attacked, routed Zhang Ya in a single fight, and Zhan Qiang’s followers surrendered in panic.

sentences.zh: 侯官既平。

translations.literal: When Houguan had been pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Houguan county was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 而建安、漢興、南平復亂，齊進兵建安，立都尉府，是歲八年也。

translations.literal: But Jian'an, Hanxing, and Nanping rebelled again; Qi advanced troops to Jian'an, established the commandant's headquarters—that year was the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jian’an, Hanxing, and Nanping exploded; He Qi marched on Jian’an, set up a command post—it was the eighth Jian’an year.

sentences.zh: 郡發屬縣五千兵，各使本縣長將之，皆受齊節度。

translations.literal: The commandery dispatched five thousand troops from subordinate counties, each county's magistrate leading his own, all receiving Qi's direction.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery drafted five thousand men from its counties, each led by its own magistrate, all under He Qi’s orders.

sentences.zh: 賊洪明、洪進、苑御、吳免、華當等五人，率各萬戶，連屯漢興，吳五六千戶別屯大潭。

translations.literal: The bandits Hong Ming, Hong Jin, Yuan Yu, Wu Mian, Hua Dang, and five others each led ten thousand households in linked camps at Hanxing; Wu had five or six thousand households separately camped at Datan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs Hong Ming, Hong Jin, Yuan Yu, Wu Mian, and Hua Dang—five bands of some ten thousand households each—linked camps at Hanxing; another five or six thousand households under Wu camped at Datan.

sentences.zh: 鄒臨六千戶別屯蓋竹，大潭同出餘汗。

translations.literal: Zou Lin had six thousand households separately camped at Gaizhu; Datan likewise issued onto Yukan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Lin’s six thousand households held Gaizhu; Datan’s force also debouched toward Yukan.

sentences.zh: 〈音干。〉

translations.literal: 〈It is read gan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The commentary notes the place name is read like “gan.”〉

sentences.zh: 軍討漢興，經餘汗。

translations.literal: The army campaigned against Hanxing, passing through Yukan.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi’s column marched on Hanxing through Yukan.

sentences.zh: 齊以為賊眾兵少，深入無繼，恐為所斷，令松陽長丁蕃留備余汗。

translations.literal: Qi thought the bandits numerous and the troops few; if he penetrated deeply without follow-up, he feared being cut off; he ordered the magistrate of Songyang, Ding Fan, to remain and guard Yukan.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing encirclement—many rebels, few men—he left Ding Fan of Songyang to hold Yukan.

sentences.zh: 蕃本與齊鄰城，恥見部伍，辭不肯留。

translations.literal: Fan had originally been in a neighboring city to Qi and was ashamed to be placed under a unit; he declined and was unwilling to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Fan, a neighboring magistrate, resented serving under He Qi’s command and refused the posting.

sentences.zh: 齊乃斬蕃，於是軍中震慄。

translations.literal: Qi then executed Fan; thereupon the army trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi executed him on the spot, and the army shook with dread.

sentences.zh: 無不用命。

translations.literal: There was none who did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every officer obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 遂分兵留備，進討明等，連大破之。

translations.literal: He then divided troops to leave guards and advanced to punish Ming and the others, in succession greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He split off detachments to guard the rear, then stormed Hong Ming’s positions and broke them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 臨陳斬明，其免、當、進、御皆降。

translations.literal: In the engagement he beheaded Ming; Mian, Dang, Jin, and Yu all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ming died on the field; Wu Mian, Hua Dang, Hong Jin, and Yuan Yu capitulated.

sentences.zh: 轉擊蓋竹，軍向大潭，三將又降。

translations.literal: He turned to strike Gaizhu, aimed the army at Datan, and the three commanders again surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He swung against Gaizhu, then Datan, and three more chiefs yielded.

sentences.zh: 凡討治斬首六千級，名帥盡擒。

translations.literal: In all the punitive campaign beheaded six thousand ranks; all the famed chiefs were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign took six thousand heads and every noted leader alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 復立縣邑，料出兵萬人，拜為平東校尉。

translations.literal: He again established counties and townships, assessed and raised ten thousand troops, and was appointed Colonel Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He refounded cantons, levied ten thousand picked soldiers, and was named Colonel Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉討上饒，分以為建平縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he turned to campaign against Shangrao and divided it to form Jianping county.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he attacked Shangrao and carved out Jianping county.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷威武中郎將，討丹陽黟、歙。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted General of the Household Gentlemen of Martial Prestige and campaigned against Yi and She in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian’an 13 brought promotion to General of the Household Gentlemen of Martial Might for the Danyang campaign against Yi and She.

sentences.zh: 時武強、葉鄉、東陽、豐浦四鄉先降，齊表言以葉鄉為始新縣。

translations.literal: At that time the four townships Wujiang, Yexiang, Dongyang, and Fengpu had surrendered first; Qi memorialized that Yexiang be made Shixin county.
translations.idiomatic: Four townships—Wujiang, Yexiang, Dongyang, and Fengpu—had already submitted; He Qi asked to make Yexiang into Shixin county.

sentences.zh: 而歙賊帥金奇萬戶屯安勒山，毛甘萬戶屯烏聊山，黟帥陳僕，祖山等二萬戶屯林歷山。

translations.literal: But the She bandit chief Jin Qi with ten thousand households camped on Mount Anle, Mao Gan with ten thousand households on Mount Wuliao, and the Yi chiefs Chen Pu and Zu Shan with twenty thousand households camped on Mount Linli.
translations.idiomatic: In She, Jin Qi camped ten thousand households on Mount Anle; Mao Gan did the same on Mount Wuliao; in Yi, Chen Pu and Zu Shan held twenty thousand on Mount Linli.

sentences.zh: 林歷山四面壁立，高數十丈，逕路危狹，不容刀楯，賊臨高下石，不可得攻。

translations.literal: Mount Linli was precipitous on four sides like a wall, several tens of ren high; paths were perilous and narrow, not admitting shield or blade; the bandits overlooking from above rolled stones—attack could not be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Linli rose like a sheer wall scores of feet high, its trails too narrow for shield or blade, while defenders rained rock from above.

sentences.zh: 軍住經日，將吏患之。

translations.literal: The army halted for days; generals and clerks worried.
translations.idiomatic: The siege stalled and the staff grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 齊身出周行，觀視形便，陰募輕捷士，為作鐵弋，密於隱險賊所不備處，以戈拓斬山為緣道，夜令潛上，乃多縣布以援下人，得上百數人，四面流布，俱鳴鼓角，齊勒兵待之。

translations.literal: Qi himself went out and made a circuit, observing the terrain for advantage; he secretly recruited agile men, had iron spears made for them, and in hidden perilous places where the bandits were unprepared used the spears to pry and cut the mountain into a path; at night he had them climb stealthily, then hung many bolts of cloth to haul men below; more than a hundred got up, spread out on four sides, and all beat drums and blew horns; Qi drew up troops awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi reconnoitered in person, forged iron crowbars, and under cover of night cut secret stairways up the cliff, hauled picked climbers on cloth ropes, then had them drum and shout from every side while his main force waited below.

sentences.zh: 賊夜聞鼓聲四合，謂大軍悉已得上，驚懼惑亂，不知所為，守路備險者，皆走還依眾。

translations.literal: The bandits in the night, hearing drum sounds converge from four sides, thought the great army had all already gotten up; they were frightened, confused, and did not know what to do; those guarding roads and defending narrows all ran back to join the mass.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders thought the whole army had gained the heights and fled toward the main camp in confusion.

sentences.zh: 大軍因是得上，大破僕等，其餘皆降，凡斬首七千。

translations.literal: The great army thereby was able to ascend, greatly broke Pu and the others, and the rest all surrendered; in all seven thousand heads were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi’s men swarmed the summit, shattered Chen Pu’s host, and took seven thousand heads; the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 〈《抱朴子》曰：昔吴遣贺将军讨山贼，贼中有善禁者，每当交战，官军刀剑不得拔，弓弩射矢皆还自向，辄致不利。

translations.literal: 〈The Baopuzi states: Formerly Wu sent General He to campaign against mountain bandits; among the bandits was one skilled in prohibitions—whenever they joined battle, government troops could not draw swords or spears, and crossbows shot arrows that all turned back on themselves, always bringing ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Baopuzi tells how Wu once sent General He against mountain rebels whose shamans “bound” metal so blades would not leave the scabbard and bowstrings drove arrows backward.

sentences.zh: 贺将军长情有思，乃曰：“吾闻金有刃者可禁，虫有毒者可禁，其无刃之物，无毒之虫，则不可禁。

translations.literal: General He, long in feeling and thought, said, "I have heard that metal that has an edge may be prohibited, and insects that have venom may be prohibited; things without edges and insects without venom cannot be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: General He reasoned: “Spells can stop edged metal and venom, not plain wood or toothless vermin.”

sentences.zh: 彼必是能禁吾兵者也，必不能禁无刃物矣。

translations.literal: " They must be able to prohibit our armed soldiers, but they surely cannot prohibit things without edges.
translations.idiomatic: “They can hex our steel; they cannot hex a club.”

sentences.zh: ”乃多作劲木白棓，选有力精卒五千人为先登，尽捉棓。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he had many strong wooden white clubs made, selected five thousand strong picked soldiers as vanguard, and had them all grasp clubs.
translations.idiomatic: He armed five thousand storm troops with heavy white-oak clubs.

sentences.zh: 彼山贼恃其有善禁者，了不严备。

translations.literal: Those mountain bandits, relying on their having one skilled in prohibitions, were altogether lax in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, trusting their wizardry, left their guard down.

sentences.zh: 於是官军以白棓击之，彼禁者果不复行，所击杀者万计。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon government troops struck them with white clubs; those prohibitionists indeed could not make it work again, and those killed and struck numbered in the tens of thousands.〉
translations.idiomatic: Government troops clubbed them until the magic failed and tens of thousands fell.〉

sentences.zh: 齊復表分歙為新定；

translations.literal: Qi again memorialized to divide She into Xinding;
translations.idiomatic: He Qi petitioned to split She commandery again—first Xinding;

sentences.zh: 黎陽、休陽。

translations.literal: Liyang and Xiuyang.
translations.idiomatic: then Liyang and Xiuyang;

sentences.zh: 並黟、歙凡六縣。

translations.literal: Together with Yi and She, six counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: with Yi and She that made six counties in all.

sentences.zh: 權遂割為新都郡，齊為太守，立府於始新，加偏將軍。

translations.literal: Sun Quan thereupon carved it as Xindu commandery; Qi became administrator, established headquarters at Shixin, and was additionally appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Side.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan formed Xindu commandery from them, made He Qi its prefect with seat at Shixin, and added the title General of the Gentlemen of the Side.

sentences.zh: 十六年，吳郡餘杭民郎稚合宗起賊，復數千人，齊出討之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the people of Yuhang in Wu commandery, Lang Zhi, united clans and raised bandits, again several thousand men; Qi went out to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Lang Zhi of Yuhang rallied clans in revolt; He Qi crushed them.

sentences.zh: 即復破稚，表言分餘杭為臨水縣。

translations.literal: At once he again broke Zhi and memorialized that Yuhang be divided into Linshui county.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Lang Zhi immediately and asked to carve Yuhang into Linshui county.

sentences.zh: 被命詣所在，及當還郡，權出祖道，作樂舞象。

translations.literal: Receiving orders to go to the place, and when he was to return to the commandery, Sun Quan came out to the road of sacrifice for travelers, setting up music and elephant dance.
translations.idiomatic: When orders took him abroad and he was due home, Sun Quan held a farewell on the highway with music and elephant dance.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：权谓齐曰：“今定天下，都中国，使殊俗贡珍，狡兽卒舞，非君谁与？

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Sun Quan said to Qi, "Now that the realm is settled and the capital is in the central plain, causing strange peoples to offer treasures and crafty beasts to end their dance—if not with you, with whom?"
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu records Sun Quan saying, “When the realm is settled at Luoyang, who but you will bring tribute beasts and foreign gifts?”

sentences.zh: ”齐曰：“殿下以神武应期，廓开王业，臣幸遭际会，得驱驰风尘之下，佐助末行，效鹰犬之用，臣之原也。

translations.literal: " Qi said, "Your Highness, in spirit and martialness answering the times, has opened wide the kingly enterprise; your servant luckily encountered the meeting and was able to gallop in the dust below, assisting in the least tasks and performing the use of hawk and hound—this is your servant's original desire.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi answered: “Your Highness’s divine arms opened the royal work; I am lucky to run before your dust like a hunting hound—that is all I wish.”

sentences.zh: 若殊俗贡珍，狡兽率舞，宜在圣德，非臣所能。”〉

translations.literal: " If strange peoples offer treasures and crafty beasts lead the dance, that ought to lie in sagely virtue; it is not what your servant can do."〉
translations.idiomatic: “As for tribute and dancing beasts—that belongs to sagely virtue, not to me.”〉

sentences.zh: 賜齊軿車駿馬，罷坐住駕，使齊就車。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Qi a light carriage and fine horses, dismissed the seated carriage he had been riding, and had Qi mount the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave him a light chariot and fine horses and made him ride in place of the heavier state carriage.

sentences.zh: 齊辭不敢，權使左右扶齊上車，令導吏卒兵騎，如在郡儀。

translations.literal: Qi declined and did not dare accept; Sun Quan had those at his sides support Qi onto the carriage and ordered the escort clerks, soldiers, and horse guards in the same ceremonial order as in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi protested; Sun Quan had attendants lift him aboard and sent him off with the full prefect’s escort.

sentences.zh: 權望之笑曰："人當努力，非積行累勤，此不可得。

translations.literal: Sun Quan watched him and laughed, saying, "A man ought to strive; without accumulated conduct and piled diligence, this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan watched him go and laughed: “Rank like that is bought only with long toil.”

sentences.zh: "去百餘步乃旋。

translations.literal: " He went more than a hundred paces and then turned back.
translations.idiomatic: He drove a hundred paces before turning back.

sentences.zh: 十八年，豫章東部民彭材、李玉、王海等起為賊亂，眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the people of the eastern division of Yuzhang, Peng Cai, Li Yu, Wang Hai, and others rose and became bandit turmoil, more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 Peng Cai, Li Yu, and Wang Hai raised ten thousand rebels in eastern Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 齊討平之，誅其首惡，餘皆降服。

translations.literal: Qi campaigned and pacified them, executed their chief evildoers, and the rest all surrendered in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi crushed them, executed the ringleaders, and accepted the rest.

sentences.zh: 揀其精健為兵，次為縣戶。

translations.literal: He picked their elite and hardy for soldiers; the next grade became county households.
translations.idiomatic: The fittest he drafted into the army; the rest registered as county taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 遷奮武將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 二十年，從權征合肥。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed Sun Quan on the expedition against Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he followed Sun Quan against Hefei.

sentences.zh: 時城中出戰，徐盛被創失矛，齊引兵拒擊，得盛所失。

translations.literal: At that time the city sortied to battle; Xu Sheng was wounded and lost his spear; Qi led troops to resist the strike and recovered what Sheng had lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei garrison sallied, Xu Sheng was wounded and dropped his spear; He Qi counterattacked and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：权征合肥还，为张辽所掩袭於津北，几至危殆。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan states: When Sun Quan campaigned against Hefei and returned, he was ambushed by Zhang Liao north of the ford and nearly reached peril and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan says Zhang Liao ambushed Sun Quan north of the crossing on the return from Hefei and nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 齐时率三千兵在津南迎权。

translations.literal: At that time Qi was leading three thousand troops south of the ford to welcome Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi waited south of the ford with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 权既入大船，会诸将饮宴，齐下席涕泣而言曰：“至尊人主，常当持重。

translations.literal: After Sun Quan had boarded the great ship, he met the various generals in drinking feast; Qi left his mat, wept, and spoke, saying, "The supreme person, lord of men, ought always to hold steady weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan gave a victory banquet aboard ship, He Qi left his cushion weeping: “A ruler must always weigh risk.”

sentences.zh: 今日之事，几至祸败，群下震怖，若无天地，原以此为终身诫。

translations.literal: " Today's affair almost reached disaster and defeat; those below were shaken in terror as if without heaven and earth; your servant begs to take this as a lifelong warning.
translations.idiomatic: “Today we brushed annihilation; the officers were blind with panic—I beg you take this as a lifelong lesson.”

sentences.zh: ”权自前收其泪曰：“大惭！

translations.literal: " Sun Quan himself came forward, gathered up his tears, and said, "Great shame!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan stepped down, wiped his tears, and said, “I am mortified.”

sentences.zh: 谨以克心，非但书诸绅也。”〉

translations.literal: " I will earnestly take it to heart—not only write it on my sash."〉
translations.idiomatic: “I will burn this into my heart, not merely tie it on my girdle.”〉

sentences.zh: 二十一年，鄱陽民尤突受曹公印綬，化民為賊，陵陽、始安、涇縣皆與突相應。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the people of Poyang, You Tu, received seal and ribbon from Duke Cao, incited the people to become bandits; Linyang, Shi'an, and Jing counties all responded to Tu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 You Tu of Poyang took a seal from Cao Cao and raised the countryside; Linyang, Shi’an, and Jing joined him.

sentences.zh: 齊與陸遜討破突，斬首數千，餘黨震服，丹楊三縣皆降，料得精兵八千人。

translations.literal: Qi together with Lu Xun campaigned, broke Tu, beheaded several thousand, and the remaining faction trembled in submission; three counties of Danyang all surrendered, and he assessed and obtained eight thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi and Lu Xun shattered the revolt, took thousands of heads, pacified Danyang’s three counties, and enrolled eight thousand veterans.

sentences.zh: 拜安東將軍，封山陰侯，出鎮江上，督扶州以上至皖。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, enfeoffed marquis of Shanyin, went out to guard the Yangzi, and supervised from Fuzhou upward to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Pacifies the East, marquis of Shanyin, and given the upper Yangzi from Fuzhou to Wan.

sentences.zh: 黃武初，魏使曹休來伐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangwu, Wei sent Cao Xiu to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangwu, Wei sent Cao Xiu against Wu.

sentences.zh: 齊以道遠後至，因住新市為拒。

translations.literal: Because Qi came late on the long road, he therefore halted at Xinshi to resist.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi arrived late and anchored the defense at Xinshi.

sentences.zh: 會洞口諸軍遭風流溺，所亡中分，將士失色，賴齊未濟，偏軍獨全，諸將倚以為勢。

translations.literal: It happened that the various armies at Dongkou suffered wind and drifting drowning; those lost were half in the middle; generals and soldiers lost color; they relied on Qi not yet having crossed—the detached army alone was whole—and the various generals leaned on it for strength.
translations.idiomatic: A storm sank half the fleet at Dongkou; only He Qi’s detachment, still on the way, remained intact, and the survivors drew courage from it.

sentences.zh: 齊性奢綺，尤好軍事，兵甲器械極為精好，所乘船雕刻丹鏤，青蓋絳襜，干櫓戈矛，葩爪文畫，弓弩矢箭，咸取上材，蒙衝鬥艦之屬，望之若山。

translations.literal: Qi's nature was luxurious and ornate; he especially loved military affairs; arms, armor, and implements were extremely fine and good; the boats he rode were carved in cinnabar and inlay, with green canopies and crimson curtains, shield racks, ge spears, floral talon patterns and painted designs, bows, crossbows, arrows, and bolts all chosen from top-grade materials; among covered swoopers and fighting ships, viewed from afar they were like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi loved splendor: lacquered warships, vermilion carving, jade-green canopies, crimson blinds, gilded arms—his squadron looked like a floating mountain range.

sentences.zh: 休等憚之，遂引軍還。

translations.literal: Xiu and the others feared them and thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu’s officers took one look and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷後將軍，假節領徐州牧。

translations.literal: He was promoted General of the Rear, lent credentials of authority, and appointed Shepherd of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Rear with credential-axe and nominal shepherd of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 初，晉宗為戲口將，以眾叛如魏，還為蘄春太守，圖襲安樂，取其保質。

translations.literal: At first Jin Zong had been general at Xikou; with his host he rebelled and went over to Wei, later became Administrator of Qichun, and plotted a surprise on Anle to take its hostage hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zong had commanded Xikou, defected to Wei, become prefect of Qichun, and plotted to raid Anle for hostages.

sentences.zh: 權以為恥忿，因軍初罷，六月盛夏、出其不意，詔齊督麋芳、鮮于丹等襲蘄春，遂生虜宗。

translations.literal: Sun Quan thought it shame and rage; because the army had just stood down, in the sixth month, midsummer, catching him off guard, he ordered Qi to supervise Mi Fang, Xianyu Dan, and others in a raid on Qichun, and they captured Zong alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, furious and shamed, struck in the sixth-month heat while Wei’s guard was slack; He Qi, Mi Fang, and Xianyu Dan took Qichun and seized Jin Zong alive.

sentences.zh: 後四年卒，子達及弟景皆有令名，為佳將。

translations.literal: Four years later he died; his sons Da and younger brother Jing both had fair reputations and were fine generals.
translations.idiomatic: He died four years later; his sons He Da and He Jing were noted commanders.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：景为灭贼校尉，御众严而有恩，兵器精饰，为当时冠绝，早卒。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: Jing was Colonel Who Extinguishes Bandits; in commanding the host he was strict yet had kindness; arms and weapons were finely adorned, foremost of the time in excellence; he died early.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu says He Jing was Colonel Who Exterminates Bandits—strict but kind, unmatched in equipping troops—yet died young.

sentences.zh: 达颇任气，多所犯迕，故虽有征战之劳，而爵位不至，然轻财贵义，胆烈过人。

translations.literal: Da was rather given to venting temper and often gave offense; therefore though he had the toil of campaigns, his noble rank did not reach high, yet he held goods lightly and prized righteousness, and his gallantry surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He Da was quick-tempered and blunt, so rank never matched his battles, yet he despised wealth and valued honor and was bolder than most.

sentences.zh: 子质，位至虎牙将军。

translations.literal: His son Zhi rose to the rank of General of the Tiger's Fang.
translations.idiomatic: His son He Zhi became General of the Tiger’s Fang.

sentences.zh: 景子邵，别有传。〉

translations.literal: Jing's son Shao has a separate biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: He Jing’s son He Shao has his own biography.〉

sentences.zh: 全琮字子璜，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Quan Zong, courtesy name Zihuang, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong, whose courtesy name was Zihuang, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父柔，漢靈帝時舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His father Rou was recommended as filial and incorrupt in the time of Emperor Ling of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan Rou earned nomination as filial and incorrupt under Han Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 補尚書郎右丞，董卓之亂，棄官歸。

translations.literal: He was supplemented as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and right aide; in the turmoil of Dong Zhuo he cast aside office and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the secretariat until Dong Zhuo’s coup, then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕從事，詔書就拜會稽東部都尉。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as aide-de-camp; an edict appointed him on the spot Commandant of the Eastern Section of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The province named him aide-de-camp; an imperial edict made him commandant of eastern Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 孫策到吳，柔舉兵先附，策表柔為丹楊都尉。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce reached Wu, Rou first raised troops and attached; Ce memorialized Rou as Commandant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce entered Wu, Quan Rou was first to rally to him; Sun Ce had him named commandant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 孫權為車騎將軍，以柔為長史，徙桂陽太守。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan was General of Chariots and Cavalry, he made Rou chief clerk and transferred him to Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan held the chariot-and-cavalry generalship he took Quan Rou as chief clerk, then sent him south as prefect of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 柔嘗使琮齎米數千斛到吳，有所市易。

translations.literal: Rou once sent Zong carrying several thousand hu of rice to Wu for some trading.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rou once dispatched Quan Zong to Wu with several thousand hu of rice to sell.

sentences.zh: 琮至，皆散用，空船而還。

translations.literal: When Zong arrived, he distributed it all in use and returned with empty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong gave every bushel away and sailed home with empty holds.

sentences.zh: 柔大怒，琮頓首曰：“愚以所市非急，而士大夫方有倒縣之患，故便振贍，不及啟報。

translations.literal: Rou was greatly angry; Zong knocked his head and said, "In folly I thought what was to be bought was not urgent, while gentlemen were suffering the distress of being hung upside down; therefore I relieved them on the spur of the moment and did not reach reporting in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rou raged; Quan Zong kowtowed and said, “The goods were not urgent, but gentlemen were starving—I fed them first and failed to ask leave.”

sentences.zh: ”柔更以奇之。

translations.literal: " Rou thereupon thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rou, reconsidering, marveled at his son.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：礼，子事父无私财，又不敢私施，所以避尊上也。

translations.literal: 〈Xu Zhong’s commentary states: By ritual a son serves his father without private wealth, nor dares private largess, thereby avoiding offense to what is exalted above.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Zhong cites ritual: a son keeps no private purse from his father.

sentences.zh: 弃命专财而以邀名，未尽父子之礼。

translations.literal: To cast aside life, monopolize wealth, and thereby seek name does not exhaust the ritual between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: To spend a father’s grain for fame strains filial duty.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为子路问“闻斯行诸？

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that when Zilu asked, "On hearing it, may one act?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes Zilu’s question: “Hear a thing—act at once?”

sentences.zh: ”子曰“有父兄在”。

translations.literal: " Confucius said, "While father and elder brothers are alive."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answered, “While father and elder brothers live.”

sentences.zh: 琮辄散父财，诚非子道，然士类县命，忧在朝夕，权其轻重，以先人急，斯亦冯暖市义、汲黯振救之类，全谓邀名，或负其心。〉

translations.literal: Zong rashly scattered his father's wealth—it is truly not the way of a son; yet the gentry hung between life and death, their worry morning and evening; weighing light and heavy, to put the urgent of others first—this is also of the kind of Feng Xuan buying righteousness or Ji An's relief—calling it wholly seeking name perhaps does his heart injustice.〉
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong’s charity was rash by Confucian reckoning, yet it matched Feng Xuan “buying righteousness” or Ji An’s relief—calling it mere fame-seeking may miss his intent.〉

sentences.zh: 是時中州士人避亂而南，依琮居者以百數，琮傾家給濟，與共有無，遂顯名遠近。

translations.literal: At that time gentlemen of the central plain fled turmoil southward; those who relied on Zong's dwelling numbered in the hundreds; Zong exhausted his household in supplying them, sharing existence and nonexistence with them, and thereby his fair name shone far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Scores of refugee scholars lodged with Quan Zong; he emptied his granaries to keep them and won fame across the southeast.

sentences.zh: 後權以為奮威校尉，授兵數千人，使討山越。

translations.literal: Later Sun Quan made him Colonel Who Rouses Might, gave him several thousand troops, and had him campaign against the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan later named him Colonel Who Rouses Might and sent him against the hill Yue with a few thousand men.

sentences.zh: 因開募召，得精兵萬餘人，出屯牛渚，稍遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon opened recruitment and summons, obtaining more than ten thousand picked troops; he went out and encamped at Niuzhu and was gradually promoted General of the Gentlemen of the Side.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited ten thousand veterans, camped at Niuzhu, and rose to side general.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，劉備將關羽圍樊、襄陽，琮上疏陳羽可討之計，權時已與呂蒙陰議襲之，恐事洩，故寢琮表不答。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, Liu Bei's general Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang; Zong submitted a memorial setting forth a plan by which Yu could be attacked; Sun Quan at that time had already secretly plotted with Lü Meng to surprise him and feared the affair would leak, therefore he suppressed Zong's memorial and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 24 Quan Zong urged a strike on Guan Yu at Fan; Sun Quan, already plotting with Lü Meng, shelved the memorial to avoid leaks.

sentences.zh: 及禽羽，權置酒公安。

translations.literal: When Yu had been captured, Sun Quan set out wine at Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Yu fell, Sun Quan feasted the army at Gong’an.

sentences.zh: 顧謂琮曰：“君前陳此，孤雖不相答，今日之捷，抑亦君之功也。

translations.literal: He turned to Zong and said, "You stated this before; though I did not answer you, today's victory is also your merit."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told him, “You warned me first; I kept silent, but this victory is yours too.”

sentences.zh: ”於是封陽華亭侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yanghua.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Quan Zong as marquis of Yanghua village.

sentences.zh: 黃武元年，魏以舟軍大出洞口，權使呂範督諸將拒之，軍營相望。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangwu, Wei sent a great fleet of boats out at Dongkou; Sun Quan sent Lü Fan to supervise the various generals in resisting them; military camps faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Huangwu 1: Wei hurled a fleet at Dongkou; Sun Quan put Lü Fan in command and the camps stared across the water.

sentences.zh: 敵數以輕船抄擊，琮常帶甲仗兵，伺候不休。

translations.literal: The enemy repeatedly used light boats to raid and strike; Zong constantly wore armor and bore arms, watching and waiting without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raiders darted in light craft; Quan Zong stayed armored on watch day and night.

sentences.zh: 頃之，敵數千人出江中，琮擊破之，梟其將軍尹盧。

translations.literal: Before long several thousand of the enemy came out into the middle of the river; Zong struck and broke them and displayed the head of their general Yin Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He caught a Wei sortie in midstream, shattered it, and took General Yin Lu’s head.

sentences.zh: 遷琮綏南將軍，進封錢唐侯。

translations.literal: Zong was promoted General Who Pacifies the South and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General Who Pacifies the South and marquis of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 四年，假節領九江太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was lent credentials of authority and appointed Administrator of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took the credential-axe and the Jiujiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，權到皖，使琮與輔國將軍陸遜擊曹休，破之於石亭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Sun Quan went to Wan, he sent Zong together with General Who Supports the State Lu Xun to strike Cao Xiu and defeated him at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7: at Wan he paired Quan Zong with Lu Xun and broke Cao Xiu at Shiting.

sentences.zh: 是時丹楊、吳、會山民復為寇賊，攻沒屬縣，權分三郡險地為東安郡，琮領太守。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain people of Danyang, Wu, and Kuaiji again became bandits and raiders, attacking and taking subordinate counties; Sun Quan divided the perilous territory of three commanderies to form Eastern Peace commandery, and Zong led as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hill folk of three commanderies revolted; Sun Quan carved out Eastern Peace commandery and put Quan Zong in charge.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：琮时治富春。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: At that time Zong administered Fuchun.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu lu says his seat was at Fuchun.〉

sentences.zh: 至，明賞罰。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he clarified rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he made rewards and punishments unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 招誘降附，數年中，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: He summoned and enticed surrender and attachment; within several years he obtained more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he enrolled another ten thousand surrendered fighters.

sentences.zh: 權召琮還牛渚，罷東安郡。

translations.literal: Sun Quan summoned Zong back to Niuzhu and abolished Eastern Peace commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then recalled him to Niuzhu and dissolved Eastern Peace commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：琮还，经过钱唐，脩祭坟墓，麾幢节盖，曜於旧里，请会邑人平生知旧、宗族六亲，施散惠与，千有馀万，本土以为荣。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan states: When Zong returned, passing Qiantang he repaired and sacrificed at tombs; banners, canopies, and insignia of office dazzled his old district; he invited meeting with townsmen, old acquaintances of a lifetime, and kin of six degrees of mourning, bestowing favors and gifts of more than a million cash—the native place took it for glory.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan describes his triumphal visit to Qiantang—sweeping tombs, parading insignia, feasting old friends, and scattering over a million cash in charity.〉

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，遷衛將軍、左護軍、徐州牧，

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong he was promoted Guard General, left protector, and Shepherd of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: Huanglong 1 made him Guard General, left protector, and nominal shepherd of Xu.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：初，琮为将甚勇决，当敌临难，奋不顾身。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: At first, when Zong was a general, he was very decisive; facing the enemy and imminent hardship, he did not spare his person.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu says young Quan Zong charged recklessly into danger.

sentences.zh: 及作督帅，养威持重，每御军，常任计策，不营小利。

translations.literal: When he became commander-in-chief, he cultivated awe and held heavy weight; whenever he commanded the army, he always relied on stratagems and did not pursue petty gains.
translations.idiomatic: As high commander he grew deliberate, trusting plans over petty spoils.

sentences.zh: 江表传曰：权使子登出征，已出军，次于安乐，群臣莫敢谏。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Sun Quan had his son Deng go out on campaign; the army had already gone out and halted at Anle, and none of the host of ministers dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan adds that when Sun Deng marched to Anle, no minister dared object—except Quan Zong.

sentences.zh: 琮密表曰：“古来太子未尝偏征也，故从曰抚军，守曰监国。

translations.literal: Zong secretly memorialized, saying, "From antiquity the heir apparent has never been sent on a separate campaign; therefore the attendant is called 'pacifying the army,' the guardian is called 'overseeing the state.'",
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in secret: “Crown princes do not lead separate armies—‘pacify the host,’ ‘oversee the capital’—that is the old rule.”

sentences.zh: 今太子东出，非古制也，臣窃忧疑。

translations.literal: " Now the heir apparent goes east—not the ancient system; your servant secretly worries and doubts."
translations.idiomatic: “To march the heir east breaks precedent; I tremble for the risk.”

sentences.zh: ”权即从之，命登旋军，议者咸以为琮有大臣之节也。〉

translations.literal: " Sun Quan immediately followed it, ordering Deng to turn the army back; those who discussed the matter all thought Zong had the integrity of a great minister.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan recalled the heir at once, and opinion credited Quan Zong with ministerly backbone.〉

sentences.zh: 尚公主。

translations.literal: He married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: He married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾二年，督步騎五萬征六安，六安民皆散走，諸將欲分兵捕之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiahe he supervised fifty thousand foot and horse in the expedition against Liu'an; the people of Liu'an all scattered and fled, and the various generals wished to divide troops to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiahe 2: he led fifty thousand men on Liu’an; the towns emptied, and subordinates wanted to hunt civilians for slaves.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：“夫乘危僥倖，舉不百全者，非國家大體也。

translations.literal: Zong said, "To ride on peril and hope for luck, where the undertaking is not one hundred percent secure, is not the great body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong refused: “Risking the army on a dice throw is not how a state should think.”

sentences.zh: 今分兵捕民，得失相半，豈可謂全哉?縱有所獲，猶不足以弱敵而副國望也。

translations.literal: " Now, if we divide troops to capture the people, gain and loss will be half each—how can that be called complete security? Even if we capture some, it is still not enough to weaken the enemy and match the state's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: “Splitting the force to round up families yields even odds at best and does not weaken Wei.”

sentences.zh: 如或邂逅，虧損非小，與其獲罪，琮寧以身受之。

translations.literal: " If we should meet mischance by accident, the loss will not be small; rather than incur blame, Zong would rather receive it on his own person.
translations.idiomatic: “If disaster strikes, the stain is mine—I will bear the blame.”

sentences.zh: 不敢徼功以負國也。”

translations.literal: " I dare not seek merit to the betrayal of the state."
translations.idiomatic: “I will not chase glory at the realm’s expense.”

sentences.zh: 赤烏九年，遷右大司馬、左軍師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chiwu he was promoted Right Grand Marshal and Left Military Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwu 9 raised him to Right Grand Marshal and Left Military Adviser.

sentences.zh: 為人恭順，善於承顏納規，言辭未嘗切迕。

translations.literal: As a person he was respectful and compliant, skilled in receiving facial expression and taking in remonstrance; his words never cut or contradicted.
translations.idiomatic: He was deferential, read Sun Quan’s mood, and couched advice so it never stung.

sentences.zh: 初，權將圍珠崖及夷州，皆先問琮。

translations.literal: At first, when Sun Quan was about to besiege Zhuya and Yizhou, he asked Zong first in each case.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Sun Quan toyed with invading Hainan or Taiwan, he asked Quan Zong first.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：“以聖朝之威，何向而不克?然殊方異域，隔絕障海，水土氣毒，自古有之，兵入民出，必生疾病，轉相污染，往者懼不能反，所獲何可多致？

translations.literal: Zong said, "With the awe of the sage court, what direction would not be conquered? Yet strange lands beyond the pale, cut off by barrier seas, have poisonous water and air—since antiquity there has been this; soldiers enter and people come out, and sickness must arise, infecting one another in turn; those who go fear they cannot return—how much can what is captured be increased?
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong answered: “Wu’s might can reach anywhere, yet offshore lands breed fever—troops land, plagues spread, and columns rarely come home rich.”

sentences.zh: 猥虧江岸之兵，以冀萬一之利，愚臣猶所不安。

translations.literal: " Basely to waste the troops on the river shore in hope of profit one in ten thousand—your foolish servant is still uneasy with this."
translations.idiomatic: “To stake the Yangzi army on a one-in-ten-thousand gain unsettles me.”

sentences.zh: ”權不聽。

translations.literal: " Sun Quan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ignored him.

sentences.zh: 軍行經歲，士眾疾疫死者十有八九，權深悔之。

translations.literal: The army marched a full year; of officers and men nine in ten died of sickness and epidemic; Sun Quan deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition lost nine men in ten to disease; Sun Quan bitterly regretted it.

sentences.zh: 後言次及之，琮對曰："當是時，群臣有不諫者，臣以為不忠。"

translations.literal: Later, when talk turned to it, Zong replied, "At that time, among the host of ministers there were those who did not remonstrate—your servant thought them disloyal."
translations.idiomatic: Later Quan Zong said flatly, “Any minister who stayed silent then was disloyal.”

sentences.zh: 琮既親重，宗族子弟並蒙寵貴，賜累千金，然猶謙虛接士，貌無驕色。

translations.literal: Zong was intimate and heavily favored; his lineage and younger male kin all received favor and nobility, gifts piling to a thousand in gold, yet he was still humble in receiving gentlemen and showed no arrogant color in demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Favor made the Quan clan rich beyond measure, yet Quan Zong stayed modest with guests.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，子懌嗣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; his son Yi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year; his son Quan Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 後襲業領兵，救諸葛誕於壽春，出城先降，魏以為平東將軍，封臨湘侯。

translations.literal: Later Yi inherited the enterprise and led troops, going to rescue Zhuge Dan at Shoucun; he was first to leave the city and surrender; Wei made him General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him marquis of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi later led relief to Shouchun, opened the gates to Wei first, and was named Pingdong general and marquis of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 懌兄子禕、儀、靜等亦降魏，皆歷郡守列侯。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother's sons Wei, Yi, Jing, and others also surrendered to Wei, all having served as prefects and ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Quan Wei, Quan Yi, Quan Jing, and others also defected to Wei and held Wei prefectures and marquisates.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：琮长子绪，幼知名，奉朝请，出授兵，稍迁扬武将军、牛渚督。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Zong's eldest son Xu was known while young, attended court audience, went out and was given troops, and was gradually promoted General Who Rouses Might and supervisor of Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu traces Quan Xu’s career to Niuzhu command.

sentences.zh: 孙亮即位，迁镇北将军。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang assumed the throne, he was promoted General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang made him General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 东关之役，绪与丁奉建议引兵先出，以破魏军，封一子亭侯，年四十四卒。

translations.literal: In the Dongguan campaign Xu together with Ding Feng proposed leading troops out first to break the Wei army; one son was enfeoffed village marquis; he died at forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongguan he and Ding Feng urged the preemptive stroke that broke Wei; one son won a village marquisate; he died at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 次子寄，坐阿党鲁王霸赐死。

translations.literal: The second son, Ji, by sitting in fawning attachment to the Prince of Lu Ba was ordered to die by gift.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Quan Ji died for backing Prince Sun Ba.

sentences.zh: 小子吴，孙权外孙，封都乡侯。〉

translations.literal: The youngest, Wu, was Sun Quan's maternal grandson and was enfeoffed marquis of Duxiang.〉
translations.idiomatic: Youngest Quan Wu, Sun Quan’s grandson-in-law, became marquis of Duxiang.〉

sentences.zh: 呂岱字定公，廣陵海陵人也，為郡縣吏，避亂南渡。

translations.literal: Lü Dai, courtesy name Dinggong, was a man of Hailing in Guangling; he was a clerk of commandery and county and fled turmoil south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai, courtesy name Dinggong, from Hailing in Guangling, fled south as a minor clerk when the north collapsed.

sentences.zh: 孫權統事，岱詣幕府，出守吳丞。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan took charge of affairs, Dai went to headquarters and went out to guard as assistant magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan’s rise brought him to headquarters, then assistant magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 權親斷諸縣倉庫及囚系，長丞皆見，岱處法應問，甚稱權意，召署錄事，出補余姚長，召募精健，得千餘人。

translations.literal: Sun Quan personally judged the granaries and prisons of the various counties; when chief and assistant magistrates were seen, Dai's handling of law matched what was asked and greatly matched Sun Quan's intent; he was summoned and attached as recorder of affairs, went out to supplement as magistrate of Yuyao, recruited picked and hardy men, and obtained more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan audited granaries and jails; Lü Dai’s rulings pleased him, so he made him recorder, then magistrate of Yuyao, where he raised a thousand picked men.

sentences.zh: 會稽東冶五縣賊呂合、秦狼等為亂，權以岱為督軍校尉，與將軍蔣欽等將兵討之，遂擒合、狼，五縣平定，拜昭信中郎將。

translations.literal: The bandits Lü He and Qin Lang of the five counties of Dongye in Kuaiji made turmoil; Sun Quan made Dai colonel of the army and together with General Jiang Qin and others led troops to campaign against them; thereupon they captured He and Lang, the five counties were pacified, and he was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Trust.
translations.idiomatic: When five eastern Kuaiji counties rose under Lü He and Qin Lang, Lü Dai led Jiang Qin, crushed them, and won the title General of Manifest Trust.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：建安十六年，岱督郎将尹异等，以兵二千人西诱汉中贼帅张鲁到汉兴寋城，鲁嫌疑断道，事计不立，权遂召岱还。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, Dai supervised Colonel Yin Yi and others with two thousand troops west to lure the bandit chief Zhang Lu of Hanzhong to Hanxing Jingcheng; Lu suspected and cut the road; the affair's plan did not stand; Sun Quan thereupon summoned Dai back.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈A Jian’an 16 probe toward Hanzhong’s Zhang Lu failed when the road was cut; Sun Quan recalled Lü Dai.〉

sentences.zh: 建安二十年，督孫茂等十將從取長沙三郡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jian'an he supervised Sun Mao and ten generals in following to take the three commanderies of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Jian’an 20: he led ten generals under Sun Mao to seize three Changsha commanderies.

sentences.zh: 又安成、攸、永新、茶陵四縣吏共入陰山城，合眾拒岱，岱攻圍，即降，三郡克定。

translations.literal: Again the clerks of the four counties Ancheng, You, Yongxin, and Chaling together entered Yinshan city, united the host, and resisted Dai; Dai attacked and besieged, and they at once surrendered—the three commanderies were taken and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of four southern counties barricaded Yinshan; Lü Dai stormed it, they yielded, and three commanderies were secured.

sentences.zh: 權留岱鎮長沙。

translations.literal: Sun Quan left Dai to guard Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan left him to hold Changsha.

sentences.zh: 安成長吳碭及中郎將袁龍等首尾關羽，復為反亂。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Ancheng, Wu Dang, and the colonel Yuan Long, among others, linked tails with Guan Yu and again made rebellious turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wu Dang and Colonel Yuan Long then colluded with Guan Yu and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 碭據攸縣，龍在醴陵。

translations.literal: Dang held You county; Long was in Liling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dang seized You; Yuan Long held Liling.

sentences.zh: 權遣橫江將軍魯肅攻攸，碭得突走。

translations.literal: Sun Quan dispatched General Who Crosses the River Lu Su to attack You; Dang obtained a breakthrough and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Lu Su against You; Wu Dang broke out.

sentences.zh: 岱攻醴陵，遂禽斬龍。

translations.literal: Dai attacked Liling, thereupon captured and beheaded Long.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai took Liling and executed Yuan Long.

sentences.zh: 遷廬陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to prefect of Luling.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，代步騭為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yankang he replaced Bu Zhi as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yankang 1 he replaced Bu Zhi as inspector of Jiao province.

sentences.zh: 到州，高涼賊帥錢博乞降，岱因承製，以博為高涼西部都尉。

translations.literal: When he reached the province, the bandit chief Qian Bo of Gaoliang begged to surrender; Dai, acting on discretionary authority, made Bo Commandant of the Western Section of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoliang chief Qian Bo surrendered; Lü Dai confirmed him as western Gaoliang commandant.

sentences.zh: 又鬱林夷賊攻圍郡縣，岱討破之。

translations.literal: Again the Yi bandits of Yulin attacked and besieged counties; Dai campaigned and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin tribes besieged towns; he broke them.

sentences.zh: 是時桂陽、湞陽賊王金合眾於南海界上，首亂為害，權又詔岱討之，生縛金，傳送詣都，斬首獲生凡萬餘人。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit Wang Jin of Guiyang and Zhenyang united the host on the border of Nanhai, took the lead in rebellion, and did harm; Sun Quan again ordered Dai to campaign against him; he captured Jin alive, sent him in bonds to the capital, and in heads taken and captives alive obtained altogether more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent him against Wang Jin on the Nanhai border; he shipped Jin to Jianye in chains with ten thousand counted kills and captives.

sentences.zh: 遷安南將軍，假節，封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Pacifies the South, lent credentials of authority, and enfeoffed marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Pacifies the South with credential-axe and marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 交阯太守士燮卒，權以燮子徽為安遠將軍，領九真太守，以校尉陳時代燮。

translations.literal: When the Administrator of Jiaozhi Shi Xie died, Sun Quan made Xie's son Hui General Who Pacifies Remote, in charge of Jiuzhen Administrator, and Colonel Chen Dai to replace Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xie died, Sun Quan named Shi Hui general over Jiuzhen and sent Chen Dai to replace the Shi line at Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 岱表分海南三郡為交州，以將軍戴良為刺史，海東四郡為廣州，岱自為刺史。

translations.literal: Dai memorialized to divide the three commanderies south of the sea into Jiaozhou, with General Dai Liang as inspector, and the four commanderies east of the sea into Guangzhou, with Dai himself as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai petitioned to split the south into Jiao and Guang provinces—Dai Liang over Jiao, himself over Guang.

sentences.zh: 遣良與時南入，而徽不承命，舉兵戍海口以拒良等。

translations.literal: He sent Liang and Chen south to enter, but Hui did not accept the command, raised troops, and garrisoned the estuary of the sea to resist Liang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hui defied the order, blocked the estuary, and faced Dai Liang.

sentences.zh: 岱於是上疏請討徽罪，督兵三千人晨夜浮海。

translations.literal: Dai thereupon submitted a memorial asking to punish Hui's crime, supervised three thousand troops, and floated on the sea morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai memorialized for punishment and took three thousand men down the coast by night.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰："徽藉累世之恩，為一州所附，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Dai, "Hui relies on the grace of accumulated generations and is attached to by a whole province—not easy to treat lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Advisers warned that Shi Hui’s family held Jiao for generations.

sentences.zh: "岱曰："今徽雖懷逆計，未虞吾之卒至，若我潛軍輕舉，掩其無備，破之必也。

translations.literal: " Dai said, "Now, though Hui harbors a rebellious plan, he has not reckoned with our sudden arrival; if our concealed army moves lightly and catches him unprepared, breaking him is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai answered: “He does not expect this speed—a sudden strike will shatter him.”

sentences.zh: 稽留不速，使得生心，嬰城固守，七郡百蠻，雲合響應，雖有智者，誰能圖之?"遂行，過合浦，與良俱進。

translations.literal: " If we delay and do not hurry, letting him give birth to a mind, garrison the city and hold fast in defense, with the seven commanderies and hundred barbarians answering like clouds and echoing like sounds—even if there were a wise man, who could scheme it?" Thereupon he went on, passed Hepu, and advanced together with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: “Delay lets him wall the city and rouse every tribe—then no planner could save us.” He sailed on, joined Dai Liang at Hepu, and struck.

sentences.zh: 徽聞岱至，果大震怖，不知所出，即率兄弟六人肉袒迎岱。

translations.literal: When Hui heard Dai had arrived, he was indeed greatly shaken in terror, did not know what to do, and thereupon led six brothers of flesh and bone, bare to the shoulders, to welcome Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hui panicked, stripped to the waist, and met Lü Dai with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 岱皆斬送其首，徽大將甘醴，桓治等率吏民攻岱，岱奮擊大破之，進封番禺侯。

translations.literal: Dai all beheaded them and sent their heads; Hui's great generals Gan Li and Huan Zhi and others led clerks and commoners in attacking Dai; Dai struck with vigor and greatly broke them; he was advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai executed them, crushed loyalist risings under Gan Li and Huan Zhi, and was advanced to marquis of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 於是除廣州，復為交州如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangzhou was abolished and it was again Jiaozhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: Guang province was folded back into Jiao.

sentences.zh: 岱既定交州，復進討九真，斬獲以萬數。

translations.literal: After Dai had settled Jiaozhou, he again advanced to campaign against Jiuzhen; beheadings and captures numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned in Jiuzhen and counted tens of thousands of kills and captives.

sentences.zh: 又遣從事南宣國化，暨徼外扶南、林邑、堂明諸王，各遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: He also sent clerks south to proclaim the civilizing influence of the state, reaching beyond the frontier to the kings of Funan, Linyi, and Tangming, each of whom dispatched envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officers to “spread civilization” until Funan, Linyi, and Tangming sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 權嘉其功，進拜鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Sun Quan praised his merit and promoted him to General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him General Who Guards the South for the feat.

sentences.zh: 黃龍三年，以南土清定，召岱還屯長沙漚口。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huanglong, because the southern soil was quiet and settled, he summoned Dai back to encamp at the Ou ford of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Huanglong 3: the south quiet, Sun Quan recalled him to Ou ford on the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 〈王隐《交广记》曰：吴后复置广州，以南阳滕脩为刺史。

translations.literal: 〈Wang Yin's Jiao Guang ji states: Wu later again established Guangzhou, with Teng Xiu of Nanyang as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wang Yin notes Wu later restored Guangzhou under Teng Xiu of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 或语脩虾须长一丈，脩不信，其人后故至东海，取虾须长四丈四尺，封以示脩，脩乃服之。〉

translations.literal: Someone told Xiu that shrimp whiskers were one zhang long; Xiu did not believe it; that person afterward deliberately went to the Eastern Sea, obtained a shrimp whisker four zhang four chi long, sealed it to show Xiu, and Xiu then believed it.〉
translations.idiomatic: A tale claims someone proved to Teng Xiu that a shrimp’s feeler could measure many feet—likely apocryphal.〉

sentences.zh: 會武陵蠻夷蠢動，岱與太常潘浚共討定之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Man and Yi of Wuling stirred foolishly; Dai together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Jun jointly campaigned and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuling tribes rose, he and Pan Jun pacified them together.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，權令岱領潘璋士眾，屯陸口，後徙蒲圻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe Sun Quan ordered Dai to lead Pan Zhang's soldiers and host, encamp at Lukou, and later was moved to Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiahe 3: Sun Quan gave him Pan Zhang’s troops at Lukou, then shifted the camp to Puqi.

sentences.zh: 四年，廬陵賊李桓、路合、會稽東冶賊隨春、南海賊羅厲等一時並起。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the bandits of Luling, Li Huan and Lu He, the bandits of Dongye in Kuaiji Sui Chun, and the bandits of Nanhai Luo Li and others rose all at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Li Huan of Luling, Sui Chun of Dongye, Luo Li of Nanhai, and others rebelled together.

sentences.zh: 權復詔岱督劉纂、唐咨等分部討擊，春即時首降，岱拜春偏將軍，使領其眾，遂為列將，桓、厲等皆見斬獲，傳首詣都。

translations.literal: Sun Quan again ordered Dai to supervise Liu Zuan, Tang Zi, and others in dividing forces to strike and attack; Chun at once came first to surrender; Dai appointed Chun General of the Gentlemen of the Side and had him lead his host, and he became a ranked general; Huan, Li, and the rest were all beheaded or captured, and heads were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Lü Dai with Liu Zuan and Tang Zi; Sui Chun surrendered at once and was made a side general under his own troops; Li Huan and Luo Li were killed or taken, their heads shipped to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 權詔岱曰：“厲負險作亂，自致梟首；

translations.literal: Sun Quan ordered Dai, saying, "Li relied on peril to make turmoil and brought on his own display of head;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote to Lü Dai: "Luo Li used the terrain and lost his head for it;

sentences.zh: 桓兇狡反覆，已降復叛。

translations.literal: Huan was fierce and cunning, turning coat repeatedly—having surrendered he rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was treacherous—he surrendered, then rose again."

sentences.zh: 前後討伐，歷年不禽，非君規略，誰能梟之？

translations.literal: Though campaigned against before and after, he was not captured for years—without your planning and strategy, who could have displayed his head?
translations.idiomatic: "Years of campaigns failed to catch him—without your strategy who could have nailed him?"

sentences.zh: 忠武之節，於是益者。

translations.literal: The integrity of loyalty and martialness was thereby the more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: "Your loyal valor shines all the brighter."

sentences.zh: 元惡既除，大小震懾，其餘細類，掃地族矣。

translations.literal: When the chief evildoers were already removed, great and small trembled in awe; the remaining petty sorts were swept away and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: "With the ringleaders gone, the rest scatter in terror."

sentences.zh: 自今巳去，國家永無南顧之虞，三郡晏然，無怵惕之驚。

translations.literal: From now on, the state will forever have no worry of looking south; the three commanderies are tranquil, without the shock of fear.
translations.idiomatic: "The south will not haunt us; three commanderies rest easy."

sentences.zh: 又得惡民以供賦役，重用歎息。

translations.literal: Again obtaining wicked people to supply labor service and levies—greatly I use sighs.
translations.idiomatic: "You also turn rebels into taxpayers—I can only sigh with relief."

sentences.zh: 賞不逾月，國之常典，制度所宜，君其裁之。”

translations.literal: Sun Quan ordered Dai, saying, "Rewards not beyond a month are the constant canon of the state; what institutions require is fitting—you shall decide it."
translations.idiomatic: "Pay the rewards within the month, as statute demands—you decide the details."

sentences.zh: 潘浚卒，岱代浚領荊州文書，與陸遜井在武昌，故督蒲圻。

translations.literal: When Pan Jun died, Dai replaced Jun in charge of Jingzhou paperwork, together with Lu Xun both being at Wuchang, formerly supervising Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Jun died Lü Dai ran Jingzhou paperwork with Lu Xun at Wuchang, still holding Puqi.

sentences.zh: 頃之，廖式作亂。

translations.literal: Before long Liao Shi made turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liao Shi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 攻圍城邑，零陵、蒼梧、鬱林諸郡騷擾，岱自表輒行，星夜兼路。

translations.literal: He attacked and besieged cities and towns; the commanderies Lingling, Cangwu, and Yulin were disturbed; Dai on his own authority memorialized to go at once, by starlight doubling the road.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged towns across Lingling, Cangwu, and Yulin; Lü Dai asked leave to march night and day.

sentences.zh: 權遣使追拜岱交州牧，及遣諸將唐咨等駱驛相繼，攻討一年破之，斬式及遣諸所偽署臨賀太守費楊等，並其支黨，郡縣悉平，復還武昌。

translations.literal: Sun Quan dispatched an envoy posthumously to appoint Dai Shepherd of Jiaozhou, and sent the various generals Tang Zi and others in continuous succession; attacking and campaigning for a year they broke them, beheaded Shi and sent the various falsely appointed ones such as Administrator of Linhe Fei Yang and the like together with their partisan cliques; commanderies and counties were all pacified, and he returned again to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him Jiao shepherd and fed in Tang Zi's columns; after a year Liao Shi fell, puppet prefect Fei Yang and allies died, the south was quiet, and Lü Dai returned to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時年已八十，然體素精勤，躬親王事。

translations.literal: At that time his years were already eighty, yet his person was always diligent in essence; he personally attended to kingly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he still ran every detail of government himself.

sentences.zh: 奮威將軍張承與岱書曰：

translations.literal: General Who Rouses Might Zhang Cheng wrote to Dai, saying,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng, General Who Rouses Might, wrote to him:

sentences.zh: 昔旦奭翼同，《二南》作歌，今則足下與陸子也。

translations.literal: Formerly Dan and Shi winged together, and the "Two Souths" made song; now it is your foot and Master Lu.
translations.idiomatic: "Dan and Shi inspired the Odes of the Two Souths; you and Lu Xun do the same today."

sentences.zh: 忠勤相先，勞謙相讓，功以權成，化與道合，君子歎其德，小人悅其美。

translations.literal: Loyal diligence putting one another first, toil and modesty yielding to one another, achievement completed by weighing, transformation joined with the Way—gentlemen sigh at your virtue, petty men delight in your beauty.
translations.idiomatic: "You rival each other in loyalty, modesty, and shared power—gentlemen admire you, commoners love you."

sentences.zh: 加以文書鞅掌，賓客終日，罷不捨事，勞不言倦。

translations.literal: Add to that paperwork in constant press, guests all day, when dismissed not setting aside affairs, in toil not speaking of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: "You drown in documents and guests yet never drop a file."

sentences.zh: 又知上馬輒自超乘，不由跨躡，如此足下過廉頗也。

translations.literal: Also knowing that when mounting a horse you always vault the mount yourself, not going by stirrup—thus, sir, you surpass Lian Po.
translations.idiomatic: "You vault the saddle like Lian Po in his prime."

sentences.zh: 何其事事決也。

translations.literal: How is it that in every affair you are so decisive?
translations.idiomatic: "How can you be so decisive in everything?"

sentences.zh: 《周易》有之，禮言恭，德言盛，足下何有盡此美耶！

translations.literal: The Zhou yi has it: in ritual one speaks of reverence, in virtue one speaks of abundance—how can you, sir, exhaust all this beauty!
translations.idiomatic: "The Classic says reverence and fullness—you own both."

sentences.zh: 及陸遜卒，諸葛恪代遜，權乃分武昌為兩部，岱督右部，自武昌上至蒲圻。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun died, Zhuge Ke replaced Xun; Sun Quan then divided Wuchang into two parts; Dai supervised the right part, from Wuchang up to Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun died Zhuge Ke split Wuchang command; Lü Dai took the right sector up to Puqi.

sentences.zh: 遷上大將軍，拜子凱副軍校尉，監兵蒲圻，孫亮即位，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted Senior General; his son Kai was appointed deputy colonel of the army, supervising troops at Puqi; when Sun Liang assumed the throne, he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior general, son Lü Kai watched Puqi, and Sun Liang named him Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 岱清身奉公，所在可述。

translations.literal: Dai kept his person pure in serving the public; wherever he was, it could be recounted.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai lived plainly for the state—every posting left a record.

sentences.zh: 初在交州，歷年不餉家，妻子饑乏。

translations.literal: At first in Jiaozhou, for successive years he did not supply his household; wife and children hungered and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiao he sent no pay home for years; his family went hungry.

sentences.zh: 權聞之歎息，以讓群臣曰：“呂岱出身萬里，為國勤事，家門內困，而孤不早知。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan heard it he sighed and blamed the host of ministers, saying, "Lü Dai went forth ten thousand li in service to the state, toiling in affairs, while within his gate there was distress, and I did not know it early.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan reproached the court: "Lü Dai served ten thousand li while his household starved, and I never knew."

sentences.zh: 股肱耳目，其責安在？

translations.literal: Where lies the responsibility of thigh, arm, eyes, and ears?"
translations.idiomatic: "Where were my eyes and ears?"

sentences.zh: ”於是加賜錢米布絹，歲有常限。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he added gifts of cash, rice, cloth, and silk, with a yearly fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted a yearly stipend of grain, silk, and cash.

sentences.zh: 始，岱親近吳郡徐原，慷慨有才志，岱知其可成，賜巾□，與共言論，後遂薦拔，官至侍御史。

translations.literal: At first Dai drew near to Xu Yuan of Wu commandery, who was high-minded and had talent and resolve; Dai knew he could be completed, bestowed headcloth and funds, and discoursed with him together; afterward he recommended and raised him, and he reached the rank of Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Xu Yuan of Wu, backed him with gifts and talk, and raised him to palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 原性忠壯，好直言，岱時有得失，原輒諫諍，又公論之，人或以告岱，岱歎曰："是我所以貴德淵者也。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was loyal and stalwart, and he loved straight speech; when Dai had gains and losses, Yuan always remonstrated sharply, and also discussed it publicly; some informed Dai, and Dai sighed, saying, "This is why I esteem Deyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan spoke bluntly on Lü Dai's faults in public; when told, Lü Dai said, "That is why I value Deyuan."

sentences.zh: "及原死，岱哭之甚哀。

translations.literal: " When Yuan died, Dai wept for him very mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Yuan died Lü Dai wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 曰：“德淵，呂岱之益友，今不幸，岱復於何聞過？

translations.literal: He said, "Deyuan was Lü Dai's beneficial friend; now unfortunately gone—where shall Dai again hear of faults?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Deyuan was the friend who corrected me—who will warn me now?"

sentences.zh: ”談者美之。

translations.literal: " Those who discussed it praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers praised the bond.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，年九十六卒，子凱嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping he died at the age of ninety-six; his son Kai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-six in Taiping 1; Lü Kai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 遣令殯以素棺，疏巾布□，葬送之制，務從儉約，凱皆奉行之。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be coffined in an unadorned coffin, with plain headcloth and coarse cloth for burial; in the system of burial and sending off, he insisted on following economy and restraint—Kai all carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a plain coffin and shroud; Lü Kai obeyed every frugal clause.

sentences.zh: 周魴字子魚，吳郡陽羨人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fang, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Yangxian in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, courtesy name Ziyu, came from Yangxian in Wu.

sentences.zh: 少好學，舉孝廉，為寧國長，轉在懷安。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was recommended as filial and incorrupt, was magistrate of Ningguo, and was transferred to Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, won filial-incorrupt nomination, governed Ningguo and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 錢唐大帥彭式等蟻聚為寇，以魴為錢唐侯相，旬月之間，斬式首及其支黨，遷丹楊西部都尉。

translations.literal: The great chief of Qiantang Peng Shi and others swarmed like ants to become bandits; Fang was made chancellor to the marquis of Qiantang; within a month or so he beheaded Shi's head and his partisan clique, and was transferred to Commandant of the Western Section of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Shi raided Qiantang, Zhou Fang as marquis's chancellor killed him within weeks and moved up to western Danyang commandant.

sentences.zh: 黃武中。

translations.literal: In the middle of Huangwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangwu era.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽大帥彭綺作亂，攻沒屬城，乃以魴為鄱陽太守，與胡綜戮力攻討，遂生禽綺，送詣武昌，加昭義校尉。

translations.literal: The great chief of Poyang Peng Qi made turmoil, attacking and taking subordinate cities; thereupon Fang was made Administrator of Poyang, and together with Hu Zong exerted strength in attacking and campaigning; thereupon they captured Qi alive and sent him to Wuchang; he was additionally appointed Colonel Who Manifests Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Qi of Poyang seized towns; Zhou Fang as prefect and Hu Zong crushed him, sent him alive to Wuchang, and won the title Colonel Who Manifests Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 被命密求山中舊族名帥為北敵所聞知者，令譎挑魏大司馬揚州牧曹休。

translations.literal: Receiving orders secretly to seek among the old clans and famed chiefs in the mountains whom the northern foe had heard of, he was to have them deceive and provoke Wei Grand Marshal and Shepherd of Yangzhou Cao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretly told to find mountain leaders known in Wei to bait Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 魴答，恐民帥小丑不足仗任，事或漏洩，不能致休，乞遣親人□箋七條以誘休。

translations.literal: Fang replied that he feared the people's chiefs were petty clowns not enough to rely on; if the affair leaked they could not bring in Xiu; he begged to send close kin with seven items in a memorial to entice Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang answered that minor chiefs might leak the plot; he asked to send kinsmen with a seven-point memorial to lure Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 其一曰："魴以千載饒幸，得備州民，遠隔江川，敬恪未顯，瞻望雲景，天實為之。

translations.literal: The first says: "Fang, by a thousand years' rare luck, has been able to be a complete commoner of the province; far separated by rivers and streams, respectful care has not yet been displayed; gazing at cloud and sun—Heaven truly does this.
translations.idiomatic: First point: "I am a humble man of Yang separated from you by rivers—Heaven alone lets me write."

sentences.zh: 精誠微薄，名位不昭，雖懷焦渴，曷緣見明?狐死首丘，人情戀本，而逼所制，奉覿禮違。

translations.literal: Sincerity is slight and thin, name and position are not clear; though harboring burning thirst, by what means can I be seen clearly? The fox dies with its head toward its mound—human feeling clings to its root—yet I am pressed by what controls me, and reverent audience violates ritual.
translations.idiomatic: "I am obscure and powerless, yet like the fox I long for home, though Wu keeps me from court."

sentences.zh: 每獨矯首西顧，未嘗不寤寐勞歎，展轉反側也。

translations.literal: Each time alone I crane my neck and look west, never not waking and sleeping with toil and sighs, tossing and turning.
translations.idiomatic: "I stare west sleepless every night."

sentences.zh: 今因隙穴之際，得陳宿昔之志，非神啟之，豈能致此!不勝翹企，萬里托命。

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of the gap in the lair, I obtain to set forth the ambition of long nights—it is not the spirits opening this; how could I reach this! Unable to bear standing on tiptoe, I entrust my life ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: "This crack in Wu's armor lets me speak my heart—I stake my life on your answer."

sentences.zh: 謹遣親人董岑、邵南等托叛奉箋。

translations.literal: I respectfully dispatch close kin Dong Cen and Shao Nan and others, pretending defection to present the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: "I send Dong Cen and Shao Nan feigning desertion."

sentences.zh: 時事變故，列於別紙，惟明公君侯垂日月之光，照遠民之趣，永令歸命者有所戴賴。"

translations.literal: Affairs of the time and changes are set out on separate paper; may the enlightened lord and marquis let fall the light of sun and moon, illumining the bent of a distant people, forever causing those who return their mandate to have something to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: "Details are on a separate sheet—shine your light on us who would submit."

sentences.zh: 其二曰："魴遠在邊隅，江汜分絕；

translations.literal: The second says: "Fang is far in a border corner; river branches cut us off;
translations.idiomatic: Second: "The Yangzi divides us;

sentences.zh: 恩澤教化，未蒙撫及，而於山谷之間，遙陳所懷，懼以大義，未見信納。

translations.literal: grace and edifying transformation have not yet received soothing reach, yet in the midst of mountains and valleys I state what I hold in my breast from afar, fearing that in great righteousness I will not be seen to be believed and taken in.
