translations.idiomatic: I have felt no Wu kindness—will you trust a voice from the hills?"

sentences.zh: 夫物有感激，計因變生，古今同揆；

translations.literal: Things have stimulus and response; plans arise from change—the same measure in ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: "Plans shift with events—that is the way of ages."

sentences.zh: 魴仕東典郡，始願已獲，銘心立報，永矣無貳。

translations.literal: Fang served in the east in charge of a commandery; my original wish was already obtained; I carved it in the heart to establish repayment—forever without two minds.
translations.idiomatic: "I ruled a Wu county and meant to repay Wu—once."

sentences.zh: 豈圖頃者中被橫譴，禍在漏刻，危於投卵，進有離合去就之宜，退有誣罔枉死之咎，雖志行輕微，存沒一節，顧非其所，能不悵然!敢緣古人，因知所歸，拳拳輸情，陳露肝膈。

translations.literal: How could I have thought that recently I suffered sudden blame, disaster in the leaking clepsydra, peril more than casting an egg—advancing there is the fitness of separating, joining, going, and staying; retreating there is the fault of false accusation and wrongful death—though my aim and conduct are slight, in preservation and destruction it is one principle; looking at it as not my place—how can I not be despondent! I dare follow the ancients in knowing where to return; with earnest heart I convey feeling and lay bare liver and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: "Then slander struck—advance or die, retreat and be framed. I choose Wei as ancients would."

sentences.zh: 乞降春天之潤，哀拯其急，不復猜疑，絕其委命。

translations.literal: I beg the moistening of spring heaven, pity and rescue my extremity, no longer harbor suspicion, and cut off my entrusting of life.
translations.idiomatic: "Pity me, drop suspicion, spare my life."

sentences.zh: 事之宣洩。

translations.literal: If the affair leaks.
translations.idiomatic: "If word leaks,"

sentences.zh: 受罪不測，一則傷慈損計，二則杜絕向化者心，惟明使君遠覽前世，矜而愍之，留神所質，速賜秘報。

translations.literal: I will suffer punishment beyond measure—on the one hand it wounds kindness and harms planning, on the second it cuts off the hearts of those who turn toward transformation; may the enlightened envoy look far at former ages, pity and mourn them, keep mind on what is pledged, and quickly grant a secret reply.
translations.idiomatic: "I die, you lose a lever on Wu, and future defectors fear to come—send a secret pledge at once."

sentences.zh: 魴當候望舉動，俟須響應。"

translations.literal: Fang shall watch for movements and wait for echoing response."
translations.idiomatic: "I will move the moment your army moves."

sentences.zh: 其三曰："魴所代故太守廣陵王靖，往者亦以郡民為變，以見譴責，靖勤自陳釋，而終不解，因立密計，欲北歸命，不幸事露，誅及嬰孩。

translations.literal: The third says: "Fang's predecessor, the former Administrator Wang Jing of Guangling, in the past also because commandery people made change was seen to be blamed and punished; Jing diligently stated himself in release, yet in the end it was not resolved; therefore he set up a secret plan, wishing to return his mandate to the north; unluckily the affair was exposed, and execution reached infants in arms.
translations.idiomatic: Third: "My predecessor Wang Jing of Guangling tried to defect to Wei, was exposed, and even babies died."

sentences.zh: 魴既目見靖事，且觀東主一所非薄，□不復厚，雖或暫捨，終見翦除。

translations.literal: Fang has both seen Jing's affair with his own eyes and observed how the eastern lord treats one place with contempt—□ is not again thick; though sometimes temporarily spared, in the end one sees clipping and removal.
translations.idiomatic: "I have watched Sun Quan's cold favor—pardon is temporary, purge final."

sentences.zh: 今又令魴領郡者，是欲責後效，必殺魴之趣也。

translations.literal: Now again ordering Fang to lead the commandery is wanting to demand later effect—the bent of surely killing Fang.
translations.idiomatic: "Putting me over Poyang is setting me up to die."

sentences.zh: 雖尚視息，憂惕焦灼，未知軀命，竟在何時。

translations.literal: Though still drawing breath, worry and fear burn within; I do not know when body and life will in the end be.
translations.idiomatic: "I breathe, yet live on borrowed hours."

sentences.zh: 人居世間，猶白駒過隙，而常抱危怖，其可言乎!惟當陳愚，重自披盡，懼以卑賤，未能採納。

translations.literal: Man dwells in the world like the white colt passing a crack; yet constantly embracing peril and terror—can it be spoken of! I ought only to state folly and again exhaust myself in disclosure; I fear that because of mean and lowly station it cannot be taken in.
translations.idiomatic: "Life is a flicker under this terror—I beg you weigh my words."

sentences.zh: 願明使君少垂詳察，忖度其言。

translations.literal: May the enlightened envoy slightly extend detailed examination and ponder the measure of these words.
translations.idiomatic: "Read me carefully."

sentences.zh: 今此郡民，雖外名降首，而故在山草，看伺空隙，欲復為亂。

translations.literal: Now the people of this commandery, though outwardly bearing the name of surrendering heads, are still in mountain grass in old status, watching for gaps and wishing again to make turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: "Poyang's people bowed in name but still lurk in the hills."

sentences.zh: 為亂之日，魴命訖矣。

translations.literal: On the day they make turmoil, Fang's life is ended.
translations.idiomatic: "When they rise again I am dead meat."

sentences.zh: 東主頃者潛部分諸將，圖欲北進。

translations.literal: The eastern lord recently secretly deployed the various generators, planning to wish to advance north.
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Quan is secretly massing for a northern push."

sentences.zh: 呂范、孫韶等入淮，全琮、朱桓趨合肥，諸葛瑾、步騭、朱然到襄陽。

translations.literal: Lü Fan, Sun Shao, and others enter the Huai; Quan Zong and Zhu Huan press on Hefei; Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Zhu Ran reach Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Fan and Sun Shao strike the Huai line; Quan Zong and Zhu Huan aim at Hefei; Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Zhu Ran toward Xiangyang."

sentences.zh: 陸議、潘璋等討梅敷。

translations.literal: Lu Yi, Pan Zhang, and others campaign against Mei Fu.
translations.idiomatic: "Lu Yi and Pan Zhang move on Mei Fu."

sentences.zh: 東主中營自掩石陽，別遣從孫奐治安陸城，修立邸閣，輦貲運糧，以為軍儲，又命諸葛亮進指關西，江邊諸將無復在者，才留三千所兵守武昌耳。

translations.literal: The eastern lord's central army itself screens Shiyang; separately he dispatched collateral grandson Fen to pacify Ancheng city, repair and establish relay lodges, cart goods and transport grain to take as military stores; again he ordered Zhuge Liang to point toward west of the Pass; the various generals along the river are none still present—only about three thousand remaining troops guard Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Quan masks Shiyang, sends Sun Fen to Ancheng depots, calls Shu's Zhuge Liang west, and leaves only three thousand men at Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 若明使君以萬兵從皖南首江渚，魴便從此率厲吏民，以為內應。

translations.literal: If the enlightened envoy will lead ten thousand troops from south of Wan to the islets at the head of the river, Fang will thereupon from this lead and urge clerks and commoners to act as inner response.
translations.idiomatic: "March ten thousand from Wan toward the isles—I will rise inside with the people."

sentences.zh: 此方諸郡，前後舉事，垂成而敗者，由無外援使其然耳；

translations.literal: The various commanderies hereabouts, in raising affairs before and after, failed on the verge of success because there was no outer aid to make it so;
translations.idiomatic: "Past risings here failed for lack of Wei spears."

sentences.zh: 若北軍臨境，傳檄屬城，思詠之民，誰不企踵?願明使君上觀天時，下察人事，中參蓍龜，則足昭往言之不虛也。"

translations.literal: if northern troops press the border and transmit summons to subordinate cities, the people who think and chant—who will not stand on tiptoe? May the enlightened envoy look up at Heaven's time, look down at human affairs, and in the middle consult milfoil and tortoise—then it is enough to show that what was said before was not empty."
translations.idiomatic: "Show a Wei host and every town will turn—read heaven, men, and oracle and you will trust me."

sentences.zh: 其四曰："所遣董岑、邵南少長家門。

translations.literal: The fourth says: "The Dong Cen and Shao Nan dispatched are young and grown in our household.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: "Dong Cen and Shao Nan grew up in my house."

sentences.zh: 親之信之，有如兒子。

translations.literal: Intimate with them and trusting them, they are like sons.
translations.idiomatic: "I trust them as sons."

sentences.zh: 是以特令□箋，托叛為辭，目語心計，不宣唇齒，骨肉至親，無有知者。

translations.literal: Therefore I especially ordered them to carry the memorial, using pretended defection as wording; eye language and heart calculation, not declared by lips and teeth—even flesh-and-bone utmost kin have none who know.
translations.idiomatic: "They carry this letter as deserters—no one, not even kin, knows the truth."

sentences.zh: 又已敕之，到州當言往降，欲北叛來者得傳之也。

translations.literal: Also I have already charged them that when they reach the province they should say they go to surrender, wishing that those who come defecting north may pass the word.
translations.idiomatic: "I told them to pose as defectors so northern agents spread the tale."

sentences.zh: 魴建此計，任之於天，若其濟也，則有生全之福。

translations.literal: Fang established this plan, entrusting it to Heaven; if it succeeds, then there is the fortune of living preservation;
translations.idiomatic: "If Heaven favors the plot I live."

sentences.zh: 邂逅洩漏，則受夷滅之禍。

translations.literal: if by mischance it leaks, then I receive the disaster of extermination.
translations.idiomatic: "If it leaks my clan dies."

sentences.zh: 常中夜仰天，告誓星辰。

translations.literal: Often at midnight I look up to Heaven and swear to the stars.
translations.idiomatic: "I swear to the stars at midnight."

sentences.zh: 精成之微，豈能上感，然事急孤窮，惟天是訴耳。

translations.literal: The subtlety of essence completing—how can it move those above? Yet the affair is urgent, alone and poor; only Heaven is the one to appeal to.
translations.idiomatic: "Can stars hear? Yet I have only Heaven."

sentences.zh: 遣使之日，載生載死，形存氣亡，魄爽恍惚。

translations.literal: On the day of dispatching the envoy, bearing life and bearing death, form remains while breath is gone, soul and vigor dazed.
translations.idiomatic: "The day I sent them I was neither alive nor dead."

sentences.zh: 私恐使君未深保明，岑、南二人可留其一，以為後信。

translations.literal: Privately I fear the envoy has not deeply guaranteed clarity; of Cen and Nan two men, one may be kept as later pledge.
translations.idiomatic: "Keep one messenger as hostage."

sentences.zh: 一□教還，教還故當言悔叛還首。

translations.literal: One □ ordered to return; when ordered to return, he should on purpose speak of repenting defection and returning to submit.
translations.idiomatic: "Send one back feigning a change of heart."

sentences.zh: 東主有常科，悔叛還者，皆自原罪。

translations.literal: The eastern lord has standing regulations: those who repent defection and return are all forgiven their crime themselves.
translations.idiomatic: "Wu forgives returning 'deserters'—so the channel stays open."

sentences.zh: 如是彼此俱塞，永無端原。

translations.literal: Thus each side is blocked off and there is never an end or origin.
translations.idiomatic: "Both sides can keep the fiction alive."

sentences.zh: 縣命西望，涕筆俱下。"

translations.literal: Hanging life, looking west, tears and brush fall together."
translations.idiomatic: "I sign this in tears."

sentences.zh: 其五曰："鄱陽之民，實多愚勁，帥之赴役。

translations.literal: The fifth says: "The people of Poyang are in truth many foolish and obstinate; when the chief drives them to labor service,
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: "Poyang folk are stubborn—

sentences.zh: 未即應人，倡之為變，聞聲響抃。

translations.literal: they do not immediately respond to others; if one initiates them to make change, they hear the sound and clap hands.
translations.idiomatic: Stir them and they riot at a rumor.

sentences.zh: 今雖降首，盤節未解，山棲草藏，亂心猶存。

translations.literal: Now though they have surrendered heads, tangled roots are not yet undone; they dwell in mountains and hide in grass; a mind for turmoil still remains.
translations.idiomatic: "They yield in name but still hide in the hills."

sentences.zh: 而今東主圖興大眾，舉國悉出。

translations.literal: And now the eastern lord plans to raise a great host and the whole state goes out.
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Quan empties the state for this drive."

sentences.zh: 江邊空曠，屯塢虛損，惟有諸刺奸耳。

translations.literal: The river border is empty and vast; stockades and forts are hollowed and weakened—only the various "sting bandits" remain.
translations.idiomatic: "The river forts are hollow—only secret-police posts remain."

sentences.zh: 若因是際而騷動此民，一旦可得更會，然要恃外援，表裡機互，不爾以往，無所成也。

translations.literal: If at this juncture one stirs these people, in one morning they can be gathered again; yet one must rely on outer aid, inner and outer working like hinge and crossbar—otherwise, proceeding thus, nothing is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: "Raise them now with Wei support and inside meets outside—or fail."

sentences.zh: 今使君若從皖道進住江上，魴當從南對岸歷口為應。

translations.literal: Now if the envoy will advance from the Wan road and halt on the river, Fang shall from the south bank at Likou act in response.
translations.idiomatic: "Camp on the river from Wan—I will answer from Likou."

sentences.zh: 若未徑到江岸，可住百里上。

translations.literal: If you do not go straight to the river bank, you may halt a hundred li above.
translations.idiomatic: "Even a halt a hundred li inland helps."

sentences.zh: 令此間民知北軍在彼，即自善也。

translations.literal: Order the people here to know that northern troops are there, and they will settle themselves.
translations.idiomatic: "Let them hear Wei is near and they will rise."

sentences.zh: 此間民非苦饑寒而甘兵寇，苦於征討，樂得北屬，但窮困舉事，不時見應，尋受其禍耳。

translations.literal: The people here are not suffering cold and hunger yet gladly taking up arms and raiders—they suffer from levies and campaigns and gladly would belong to the north; only in distress they raise affairs and do not see response in time, soon afterward receiving disaster.
translations.idiomatic: "They hate Wu's drafts, not cold—give them a Wei signal in time."

sentences.zh: 如使石陽及青、徐諸軍首尾相銜，牽綴往兵，使不得速退者，則善之善也。

translations.literal: If you cause Shiyang and the various armies of Qing and Xu to link head and tail, tying and delaying the troops gone forth so they cannot withdraw quickly—then good within good.
translations.idiomatic: "Pin Sun Quan's host with Qing–Xu troops and the trap is perfect."

sentences.zh: 魴生在江、淮，長於時事，見其便利，百舉百捷，時不再來，敢布腹心。"

translations.literal: Fang was born between the Jiang and the Huai, grew up in affairs of the times, sees what is convenient for them—hundred undertakings, hundred victories; the time does not come twice; I dare spread belly and heart."
translations.idiomatic: "I know the Huai–Yang ground—strike once, for the moment will not return."

sentences.zh: 其六曰："東主致恨前者不拔石陽，今此後舉，大合新兵，並使潘浚發夷民，人數甚多，聞豫設科條，當以新羸兵置前，好兵在後，攻城之日。

translations.literal: The sixth says: "The eastern lord harbors resentment that formerly he did not take Shiyang; in this later undertaking he greatly combines new troops and also has Pan Jun draft Yi people—the numbers are very great; I hear that in advance he has set statutes and articles, intending to place new weak troops in the front and good troops in the rear—on the day of attacking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: "Sun Quan still smarts over Shiyang—this time he masses green recruits and Pan Jun's tribesmen ahead, veterans behind, for the storm."

sentences.zh: 雲欲以羸兵填塹，使即時破，雖未能然，是事大趣也。

translations.literal: He wishes to use weak troops to fill the ditches so that they may be broken at once; though it may not succeed so, the drift of the affair is great.
translations.idiomatic: He plans to drive expendable men into the trenches to die fast—even if that fails, the thrust of his plan is clear.

sentences.zh: 私恐石陽城小，不能久留往兵，明使君速垂救濟，試宜疾密。

translations.literal: Privately I fear Shiyang city is small and cannot long detain the troops that have gone; may the enlightened envoy quickly extend rescue and relief—it is fitting to be swift and secret.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Shiyang is too slight to hold your army long—come quickly and quietly.

sentences.zh: 王靖之變，其鑒不遠。

translations.literal: The change of Wang Jing—its mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing’s fate is the lesson still in view.

sentences.zh: 今魴歸命，非復在天，正在明使君耳。

translations.literal: Now Fang returns his mandate—no longer lies with Heaven; it lies squarely with the enlightened envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I live or die is no longer fate—it is your choice.

sentences.zh: 若見救以往，則功可必成，如見救不時，則與靖等同禍。

translations.literal: If I see rescue going forward, then merit can be surely completed; if rescue is not timely, I share Jing's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: March in time and we win; arrive late and you bury me with Wang Jing.

sentences.zh: 前彭綺時，聞旗麾在逢龍，此郡民大小歡喜，並思立效，若留一月日間，事當大成，恨去電速，東得增眾專力討綺，綺始敗耳。

translations.literal: At the time of Peng Qi before, I heard banners were at Fenglong; the people of this commandery, great and small, rejoiced together and all wished to establish merit; if you had stayed a month, the affair would have greatly succeeded—I hate that you left swift as lightning; the east was able to increase troops and concentrate strength to punish Qi, and only then did Qi begin to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Qi rose, rumor said your banners touched Fenglong—every household cheered; had Wei stayed one month the revolt would have matured, but your column vanished like lightning and Wu poured reinforcements on Peng Qi until he broke.

sentences.zh: 願使君深察此言。"

translations.literal: May the envoy deeply examine these words."
translations.idiomatic: Read these lines with care."

sentences.zh: 其七曰："今舉大事，自非爵號無以勸之，乞請將軍、侯印各五十紐，郎將印百紐，校尉、都尉印各二百紐，得以假授諸魁帥，獎厲其志，並乞請幢麾數十，以為表幟，使山兵吏民，目瞻見之，知去就之分己決，承引所救畫定。

translations.literal: The seventh says: "Now in raising a great affair, unless there are noble ranks there is no means to encourage them; I beg fifty cords each of general and marquis seals, one hundred cords of lang-jiang seals, two hundred each of colonel and commandant seals, so as to be able to lend them in false grant to the various chieftains, encouraging their aims; and I beg several tens of banners and standards to serve as markers, so that mountain soldiers, clerks, and common people, seeing them with their eyes, know that the division between going and staying is already decided and the relief you extend is drawn firm.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: “Offer blank seals—fifty general and marquis ribbons, a hundred lang-jiang, two hundred colonel and commandant—so I can fake commissions to chiefs, plus dozens of banners so hill folk see which side is fixed.”

sentences.zh: 又彼此降叛，日月有人，闊狹之間，輒得聞知。

translations.literal: Again, on both sides those who surrender and rebel are daily someone; in the space between wide and narrow one always gets to hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters cross the line every day—news still reaches me.

sentences.zh: 今之大事，事宜神密，若省魴箋，乞加隱秘。

translations.literal: Now the great affair ought to be spirit-like and secret; if you have perused Fang's memorial, I beg you add secrecy to it."
translations.idiomatic: Burn this after reading—secrecy is everything."

sentences.zh: 伏知智度有常，防慮必深，魴懷憂震灼，啟事蒸仍，乞未罪怪。"

translations.literal: I know your wisdom and measure have constancy and precaution must be deep; Fang harbors worry burned within and submits affairs repeatedly by steam—I beg you not yet blame or find strange."
translations.idiomatic: I nag because I burn with fear—forgive the clutter."

sentences.zh: 魴因別為密表曰：

translations.literal: Fang thereupon separately made a secret memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang also filed a sealed memorial:

sentences.zh: 方北有逋寇，固阻河洛，久稽王誅，自擅朔土，臣曾不能吐奇舉善。

translations.literal: Just now the north has a fleeing foe, firmly blocking the He and Luo, long delaying the king's punishment, monopolizing the northern soil—your servant has been unable to spit forth wonders and raise the good.
translations.idiomatic: Wei still clogs the Central Plain and mocks the throne—yet I have done nothing brilliant for you.

sentences.zh: 上以光贊洪化，下以輸展萬一，憂心如搗，假寐忘寢。

translations.literal: Above to brighten and assist the vast transformation, below to extend in submission the one in ten thousand—worry is like pounding, in feigned sleep forgetting sleep.
translations.idiomatic: I should magnify your sage rule yet I toss awake, useless as I am.

sentences.zh: 聖朝天覆，含臣無效，猥發優命。

translations.literal: The sage court covers like heaven, containing your servant without effect, yet basely issuing a generous command.
translations.idiomatic: You cover me like heaven though I deserve nothing.

sentences.zh: 敕臣以前誘致賊休，恨不如計，令於郡界求山谷魁帥為北賊所聞知者。

translations.literal: It charged your servant earlier to lure in the bandit Xiu; I hate that the plan did not match, and now within the commandery boundary seeks mountain-valley chieftains whom the northern foe has heard of.
translations.idiomatic: You first asked me to bait Cao Xiu; that failed, so you ordered me to find bandit chiefs Wei would recognize.

sentences.zh: 令與北通。

translations.literal: Ordering them to communicate with the north.
translations.idiomatic: Men who can talk to Wei.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思惟，喜怖交集。

translations.literal: Your servant has knelt and pondered, joy and terror mingled.
translations.idiomatic: I am both grateful and terrified.

sentences.zh: 竊恐此人不可卒得，假使得之，懼不可信，不如令臣譎休，於計為便。

translations.literal: Privately I fear such men cannot be got in haste; granting one could get them, I fear they could not be trusted—it is not as good as ordering your servant to deceive Xiu, which in planning is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Those cutthroats are scarce and untrustworthy—better let me play Cao Xiu myself.

sentences.zh: 此臣得以經年之冀願。

translations.literal: This is what your servant has been able to hope for through the years.
translations.idiomatic: That has been my prayer for years.

sentences.zh: 逢值千載之一會，輒自督竭，竭盡頑蔽，撰立箋草以誑誘休者，如別紙。

translations.literal: Encountering a meeting of one in a thousand ages, I then personally supervise exhaustion, exhaust stubborn dullness, compose memorial drafts to beguile Xiu, as on separate paper.
translations.idiomatic: This once-in-an-age chance makes me draft the seven letters you hold.

sentences.zh: 臣知無古人單復之術，加卒奉大略，伀矇狼狽，懼以輕愚，忝負特施。

translations.literal: Your servant knows he lacks the ancients' arts of single combat and repetition; moreover suddenly receiving the great outline, muddled and in a flurry, I fear that in light foolishness I may shamefully fail the special application.
translations.idiomatic: I am no ancient hero—sudden duty leaves me clumsy and afraid of failing you.

sentences.zh: 豫懷憂灼。

translations.literal: I beforehand harbor worry burned within.
translations.idiomatic: I tremble beforehand.

sentences.zh: 臣聞唐堯先天而天弗違，博詢芻蕘，以成盛勳。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Tang Yao was before Heaven and Heaven did not oppose, broadly inquiring of grass and firewood cutters to complete great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao asked woodcutters—I am far less.

sentences.zh: 朝廷神謨，欲必致休於步度之中，靈贊聖規，休必自送，使六軍囊括，虜無孑遺，威風電邁，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: The court's spirit-like plan desires surely to bring Xiu within the stride of the plan; spirits assist the sage compass, and Xiu will surely deliver himself, letting the six armies bag and pocket him so captives have not even a leftover—awe-inspiring wind and lightning march—great fortune for the world.
translations.idiomatic: Your strategists mean to bag Cao Xiu in one cast of the net—Heaven will help, and Wei will lose an army.

sentences.zh: 謹拜表以聞，並呈箋草，懼於淺局，追用悚息。

translations.literal: I respectfully bow the memorial to inform, and present the memorial drafts; I fear shallow scope and pursue use with shuddering breath.
translations.idiomatic: I enclose the bait-text and beg you overlook my shallow wit.

sentences.zh: 被報施行。

translations.literal: Receiving reply, it was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and ran with it.

sentences.zh: 休果信魴，帥步騎十萬，輜重滿道，逕來入皖。

translations.literal: Xiu indeed trusted Fang, leading foot and horse in the tens of thousands, baggage trains filling the road, coming straight to enter Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu swallowed the tale and marched tens of thousands, wagons jamming the roads, straight for Wan.

sentences.zh: 魴亦合眾，隨陸遜橫截休，休幅裂瓦解，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Fang also united the host, following Lu Xun in crosswise interception of Xiu; Xiu split and crumbled like cloth, beheadings and captures numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang joined Lu Xun across his path and shattered him—countless heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 魴初建密計時，頻有郎官奉詔詰問諸事，魴乃詣部郡門下，因下發謝，故休聞之，不復疑慮。

translations.literal: When Fang first set up the secret plan, frequently there were gentlemen of the Lang office bearing edicts to question various matters; Fang then went to the gate under the ministry commandery, and thereupon let down hair in apology—therefore Xiu heard it and no longer doubted.
translations.idiomatic: While the plot brewed, court officers questioned Zhou Fang; he shaved his head at the prefecture gate in mock disgrace so Cao Xiu would trust the defection.

sentences.zh: 事捷軍旋，權大會諸將歡宴，酒酣。

translations.literal: When the affair succeeded and the army returned, Sun Quan greatly assembled the various generators in a merry feast; wine ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory Sun Quan feasted his generals deep into their cups.

sentences.zh: 謂魴曰：“君下發載義，成孤大事，君之功名，當書之竹帛。

translations.literal: He said to Fang, "You let down hair bearing righteousness, completing my great affair; your merit and fame ought to be written on bamboo and silk."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told him, “You shamed yourself for the realm—your name belongs on silk.”

sentences.zh: ”加裨將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " He was additionally appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Side and enfeoffed with noble rank within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They added the title side general and marquis of the interior.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：夫人臣立功效节，虽非一涂，然各有分也。

translations.literal: 〈Xu Zhong's commentary states: When a minister establishes merit and sets integrity, though it is not one path, yet each has its allotment.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Zhong: duty takes many forms.

sentences.zh: 为将执桴鼓，则有必死之义，志守则有不假器之义，死必得所，义在不苟。

translations.literal: To be a general holding drum and mallet is to have the righteousness of certain death; to hold fast in determination is to have the righteousness of not borrowing tools; death must gain its proper place—righteousness lies in not recklessness.
translations.idiomatic: A general beats the drum ready to die; a garrison commander holds without borrowed gear—death must mean something.

sentences.zh: 鲂为郡守，职在治民，非君所命，自占诱敌，髡剔发肤，以徇功名，虽事济受爵，非君子所美。〉

translations.literal: Fang was commandery guardian; his office lay in governing the people—it was not what the lord commanded, yet on his own he undertook to lure the foe, shaving hair and skin to pursue merit and fame; though the affair succeeded and he received noble rank, it is not what the gentleman esteems.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang was a prefect, not ordered to mutilate himself for espionage—success bought rank but not every moralist approves.〉

sentences.zh: 賊帥董嗣負阻劫鈔，豫章、臨川並受其害。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Dong Si relied on obstruction and plundered; Yuzhang and Linchuan both received his harm.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Dong Si raided Yuzhang and Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：孙亮太平二年始立临川郡，是时未有临川。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi notes: Sun Liang's Taiping second year first established Linchuan commandery—at this time there was not yet Linchuan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes Linchuan did not exist yet—that name is anachronistic.〉

sentences.zh: 吾粲、唐咨嘗以三千兵攻守，連月不能拔。

translations.literal: Wu Can and Tang Zeng once with three thousand troops attacked and defended, connecting months unable to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can and Tang Zi besieged him three thousand strong for months in vain.

sentences.zh: 魴表乞罷兵，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Fang memorialized begging to stop arms, obtaining discretionary authority to act.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang asked to lift the siege and act on his own.

sentences.zh: 魴遣間諜，授以方策，誘狙殺嗣。

translations.literal: Fang dispatched spies, handing them stratagems, enticing and assassinating Si.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents with a ruse and had Dong Si killed.

sentences.zh: 嗣弟怖懼，詣武昌降於陸遜，乞出平地，自改為善，由是數郡無復憂惕。

translations.literal: Si's younger brother in fear went to Wuchang to surrender to Lu Xun, begging to come out to flat ground and from himself change to doing good—whereby several commanderies had no more worry or fear.
translations.idiomatic: The brother surrendered to Lu Xun, moved the band to the plains, and several counties slept again.

sentences.zh: 魴在郡十三年卒，賞善罰惡。

translations.literal: Fang died in the commandery after thirteen years, rewarding good and punishing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years as prefect he died, rewarding good and punishing evil.

sentences.zh: 威恩並行。

translations.literal: Might and grace went in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Awe and kindness worked together.

sentences.zh: 子處，亦有文武材干，天紀中為東觀今、無難督。

translations.literal: His son Chu also had civil and military talent and capacity; in the years of Tianji he was director of the Eastern Institute and Commandant Without Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Chu had talent; under Jin he became Eastern Institute director and Commandant Without Difficulty.

sentences.zh: 〈《虞预晋书》曰：处入晋，为御史中丞，多所弹纠，不避强御。

translations.literal: 〈The Jin shu of Yu Yu states: When Chu entered Jin he became Palace Secretary to the Imperial Secretariat, impeaching much and not avoiding the mighty.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yu Yu’s Jin shu: Zhou Chu in Jin censored the mighty as palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 齐万年反，以处为建威将军，西征，众寡不敌，处临陈慷慨，奋不顾身，遂死於战场，追赠平西将军。

translations.literal: When Qi Wannian rebelled, they made Chu General Who Establishes Might for the western expedition; the host was few and not a match; Chu, facing the line, was high-minded and generous, not sparing his person, and therefore died on the battlefield; posthumously he was advanced General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Against Qi Wannian he took the title General Who Establishes Might, fought outnumbered, died in battle, and was posthumously named General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 处子飏、札，皆有才力，中兴之初，并见宠任。

translations.literal: Chu's sons Yang and Zha both had talent and strength; at the beginning of the Restoration both saw favor and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhou Yang and Zhou Zha were talented and favored at the Eastern Jin restoration.

sentences.zh: 其诸子侄悉处列位，为扬土豪右，而札凶淫放恣，为百姓所苦。

translations.literal: His various sons and nephews were all in ranked positions, becoming powerful gentry of Wu—while Zha was fierce, dissolute, and unrestrained, a suffering to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The clan filled offices and dominated Yangzhou until Zhou Zha’s brutality turned the people against them.

sentences.zh: 泰宁中，王敦诛之，灭其族。〉

translations.literal: In Taining, Wang Dun executed them and extinguished the clan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun wiped the line out in the Taining era.〉

sentences.zh: 鍾離牧

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu

sentences.zh: 鍾離牧字子幹，會稽山陰人，漢魯相意七世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu, courtesy name Zigan, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji, seventh-generation descendant of Han Lu minister Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu, courtesy name Zigan, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji—seventh generation from Han’s Lu minister Zhongli Yi.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧父绪，楼船都尉，兄骃，上计吏，少与同郡谢赞、吴郡顾谭齐名。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: Mu's father Xu was Commandant of Tower Ships; elder brother Yin was clerk for the capital accounts; in youth he was of the same fame as Xie Zan of the same commandery and Gu Tan of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu names his father Xu, brother Yin, and boyhood rivals Xie Zan and Gu Tan.

sentences.zh: 牧童龀时号为迟讷，骃常谓人曰：“牧必胜我，不可轻也。

translations.literal: In Mu's childhood he was nicknamed slow and tongue-tied; Yin often said to people, "Mu is sure to surpass me—do not treat him lightly."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy they called him slow; his brother said, “He will outstrip me—do not slight him.”

sentences.zh: ”时人皆以为不然。〉

translations.literal: " The people of the time all thought it was not so.〉
translations.idiomatic: Listeners laughed—later they learned better.〉

sentences.zh: 少爰居永興，躬自墾田，種稻二十餘畝。

translations.literal: In youth he loved to dwell at Yongxing, personally opening fields and planting more than twenty mu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Young Mu farmed twenty mu at Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 臨熟，縣民有識認之。

translations.literal: When it was nearly ripe, a county commoner who recognized it claimed it.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor claimed the ripening crop.

sentences.zh: 牧曰：“本以田荒，故墾之耳。

translations.literal: Mu said, "Originally because the field was waste, therefore I opened it."
translations.idiomatic: Mu said, “The plot was fallow—that is why I cleared it.”

sentences.zh: ”遂以稻與縣人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave the rice to the county man.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the whole harvest to the man.

sentences.zh: 縣長聞之，召民繋獄，欲繩以法，牧為之請。

translations.literal: When the county chief heard it, he summoned the commoner and bound him in prison, wishing to apply the law by rope; Mu for him pled.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate jailed the farmer; Mu interceded.

sentences.zh: 長曰：“君慕承宮，自行義事，

translations.literal: The chief said, "You admire Gong of Chen and on your own do righteous deeds,
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate said, “You imitate Gong Shaozi—”

sentences.zh: 〈《续汉书》曰：宫字少子，琅邪人，尝在蒙阴山中耕种禾黍，临熟，人就认之，宫便推与而去，由是发名，位至左中郎将、侍中。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xu Han shu states: Gong, courtesy name Shaozi, was a man of Langya; he once planted millet in Mengyin mountain; when it was nearly ripe, someone came and claimed it; Gong then pushed it to him and left—thereby his fame arose; he reached the ranks of Left Colonel of the Gentlemen of the Household and Palace Attendant.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Han shu cites the hermit Gong who gave away his grain.〉

sentences.zh: 僕為民主，當以法率下，何得寢公憲而從君邪？

translations.literal: I, being master for the people, ought to lead those below by law—how can I sleep on public statute and follow you?
translations.idiomatic: —but I rule by law, not by your whim.”

sentences.zh: ”牧曰：“此是郡界，緣君意顧，故來蹔住。

translations.literal: " Mu said, "This is the commandery boundary; because of the lord's intent and regard I therefore came to dwell temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: Mu answered, “I lodge here only by your courtesy.”

sentences.zh: 今以少稻而殺此民，何心復留？

translations.literal: Now to kill this commoner for a little rice—what heart would I have to remain?
translations.idiomatic: Kill a man over a few sheaves and I leave forever.”

sentences.zh: ”遂出裝，還山陰，長自往止之，為釋繋民。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he packed baggage and returned to Shanyin; the chief himself went to stop him and for him released the bound commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He packed for Shanyin; the magistrate ran after him, freed the farmer, and begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 民慚懼，率妻子舂所取稻得六十斛米，送還牧，牧閉門不受。

translations.literal: The commoner was ashamed and afraid, leading wife and children to pound the rice taken and obtained sixty hu of polished rice, sent it back to Mu; Mu closed the gate and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The family threshed sixty hu to repay him; he shut his gate.

sentences.zh: 民輸置道旁，莫有取者。

translations.literal: The people transported and left it by the road; none took it.
translations.idiomatic: They left the sacks in the lane—no one touched them.

sentences.zh: 牧由此發名。

translations.literal: Thereby Mu's fair name arose.
translations.idiomatic: His name spread from that deed.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：牧蹈长者之规。

translations.literal: 〈Xu Zhong's commentary states: Mu trod the rule of the elder.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Zhong calls him long on elder virtue.

sentences.zh: 问者曰：“如牧所行，犯而不校，又从而救之，直而不有，又还而不受，可不谓之仁让乎哉？

translations.literal: The questioner said, "As Mu did, being offended yet not checking, yet moreover saving him, straight yet not possessing, yet moreover returning yet not accepting—can it not be called benevolent yielding?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked whether turning the other cheek was true benevolence.

sentences.zh: ”答曰：“异乎吾所闻。

translations.literal: " The answer said, "It differs from what I heard.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: “Not what I call benevolence.”

sentences.zh: 原宪之问於孔子曰：‘克伐怨欲不行焉，可以为仁乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Xian asked Confucius, 'If aggression, bragging, resentment, and greed do not arise in him, can he be deemed benevolent?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian asked whether a man without malice was humane.

sentences.zh: ’孔子曰：‘可以为难矣，仁则吾不知也。

translations.literal: ' Confucius said, 'That can be called difficult; as for benevolence, I do not know.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that was merely hard—not necessarily humane.

sentences.zh: ’‘恶不仁者，其为仁矣。

translations.literal: ' 'To hate the not benevolent is for him benevolence.'
translations.idiomatic: “To hate the inhumane is humanity.”

sentences.zh: ’今小民不展四体，而认人之稻，不仁甚矣，而牧推而与之，又救其罪，斯为让非其义，所救非人，非所谓恶不仁者。

translations.literal: ' Now the little people do not stretch their four limbs yet claim another's rice—nothing is more not benevolent, yet Mu pushes it to them and moreover saves them from crime—this is yielding not in its right meaning, the rescue not the right people—not what is called hating the not benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: The thief who steals rice is deeply wrong—rewarding him is not humane.

sentences.zh: 苟不恶不仁，安得为仁哉！

translations.literal: If one does not hate the not benevolent, how can it be called benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: Without hatred of evil there is no humanity.

sentences.zh: 苍梧浇娶妻而美，让於其兄；

translations.literal: The Jiao fellow Jiao took a wife who was beautiful and yielded her to his elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao of Cangwu gave his beautiful wife to his brother—

sentences.zh: 尾生笃信，水至不去而死；

translations.literal: Wei Sheng was steeped in faith, and when the water came did not leave and died;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng drowned keeping a tryst—

sentences.zh: 直躬好直，证父攘羊；

translations.literal: Zhi Gong loved straightness, testifying that his father stole a sheep;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Gong shopped his father for a sheep—

sentences.zh: 申鸣奉法，尽忠於君而执其父。

translations.literal: Shen Ming upheld the law, being utterly loyal to the lord yet seizing his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ming arrested his own father for the law—

sentences.zh: 忠信直让，此四行者，圣贤之所贵也。

translations.literal: Loyalty, faith, straightness, yielding—these four conducts are what sages and worthies esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The classics praise four virtues—

sentences.zh: 然不贵苍梧之让，非让道也；

translations.literal: Yet they do not esteem Jiao's yielding—it is not the way of yielding;
translations.idiomatic: —yet they condemn Jiao’s “yield,”

sentences.zh: 不取尾生之信，非信所也；

translations.literal: they do not take Wei Sheng's faith—it is not what faith applies to;
translations.idiomatic: reject Wei Sheng’s “faith,”

sentences.zh: 不许直躬之直，非直体也；

translations.literal: they do not allow Zhi Gong's straightness—it is not the substance of straightness;
translations.idiomatic: disown Zhi Gong’s “honesty,”

sentences.zh: 不嘉申鸣之忠，非忠意也。

translations.literal: they do not praise Shen Ming's loyalty—it is not the intent of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: and fault Shen Ming’s “loyalty.”

sentences.zh: 今牧犯而不校，还而不取，可以为难矣，未得为仁让也。

translations.literal: Now Mu, being offended yet not checking, returning yet not accepting, can be called difficult; he has not attained benevolent yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu’s forbearance is rare, not necessarily humane yielding.

sentences.zh: 夫圣人以德报德，以直报怨，而牧欲以德报怨，非也。

translations.literal: The sage repays virtue with virtue and repays grievance with straightness—yet Mu wishes to repay grievance with virtue—this is not right.
translations.idiomatic: The sage repays injury with justice, not with gifts—Mu repaid theft with grain.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，二者何从？

translations.literal: If one must choose between the two, from which do I follow?
translations.idiomatic: Forced to choose—

sentences.zh: 吾从孔子也。”〉

translations.literal: I follow Confucius."〉
translations.idiomatic: I side with Confucius.”〉

sentences.zh: 赤烏五年，從郎中補太子輔義都尉，遷南海太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was supplemented from Gentleman of the Palace to Chief Commandant for Supporting Righteousness of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwu 5: from palace gentleman to heir’s chief commandant, then prefect of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：高凉贼率仍弩等破略百姓，残害吏民，牧越界扑讨，旬日降服。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: The Gaoliang bandit chief Reng Nu and others broke and plundered the hundred surnames, cruelly injuring clerks and common people; Mu crossed the boundary in sudden attack and in ten days surrendered them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈He crossed into Gaoliang and pacified Reng Nu in ten days.

sentences.zh: 又揭阳县贼率曾夏等众数千人，历十馀年，以侯爵杂缯千匹，下书购募，绝不可得。

translations.literal: Again the Jieyang bandit chief Zeng Xia and others had a host of several thousand men for more than ten years; with marquis rank and a thousand bolts of mixed silks, edicts went down offering purchase and reward, yet absolutely they could not be got.
translations.idiomatic: Jieyang’s Zeng Xia mocked years of wanted posters and bounties.

sentences.zh: 牧遣使慰譬，登皆首服，自改为良民。

translations.literal: Mu dispatched envoys to console and instruct; Zeng Xia and his band all submitted, from themselves changing to good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu talked them down; they shaved their rebellion and became farmers.

sentences.zh: 始兴太守羊衜与太常滕胤书曰：“锺离子幹吾昔知之不熟，定见其在南海，威恩部伍，智勇分明，加操行清纯，有古人之风。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Shixing Yang Dao wrote to Grand Master of Ceremonies Teng Yin, saying, "Zhongli Zigan I formerly knew him not thoroughly; fixing eyes on him in Nanhai, might and grace order the ranks, wisdom and courage clear-cut, plus conduct pure and clean, having the wind of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao wrote Teng Yin: “I did not know Mu—now I see him rule Nanhai with clean awe.”

sentences.zh: ”其见贵如此。

translations.literal: " He was valued thus.
translations.idiomatic: Peers esteemed him so.

sentences.zh: 在郡四年，以疾去职。〉

translations.literal: After four years in the commandery he left office because of illness.〉
translations.idiomatic: He resigned ill after four years.〉

sentences.zh: 還為丞相長史，轉司直，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Returning he became chief clerk to the Chancellor, transferred to Director of Rectitude, promoted Prefect of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he rose chief clerk, director of rectitude, then prefect of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會建安、鄱陽、新都三郡山民作亂，出牧為監軍使者，討平之。

translations.literal: It happened that the mountain people of Jian'an, Poyang, and Xindu made turmoil; he went out as Envoy of the Supervising Army and campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When three commanderies’ hill folk rose, he went as army overseer and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 賊帥黃亂、常俱籌出其部伍，以充兵役。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Huang Luan and Chang Ju led out their units to fill military service.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Huang Luan and Chang offered their bands for the register.

sentences.zh: 封秦亭侯，拜越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Qinting village and appointed Colonel of Carriage-and-Horse Who Crosses at a Gallop.
translations.idiomatic: They ennobled him marquis of Qinting and named him colonel of the swift-cavalry guard.

sentences.zh: 永安六年，蜀併於魏，武陵五谿夷與蜀接界。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongan, Shu was annexed by Wei; the Yi of the five streams in Wuling bordered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan 6: Shu fell to Wei, and Wuling’s five-streams tribes touched the old Shu frontier.

sentences.zh: 時論懼叛亂，乃以牧為平魏將軍，領武陵太守，往之郡。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time feared rebellion; thereupon Mu was made General Who Pacifies Wei and appointed Administrator of Wuling, and he went to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Court rumor foretold revolt, so Wu made Zhongli Mu General Who Pacifies Wei and sent him to Wuling.

sentences.zh: 魏遣漢葭縣長郭純試守武陵太守，率涪陵民入蜀遷陵界，屯於赤沙，誘致諸夷邑君，或起應純，又進攻酉陽縣，郡中震懼。

translations.literal: Wei dispatched the magistrate of Hanjia, Guo Chun, as acting Administrator of Wuling, led the people of Fuling into Shu territory at Qianling, encamped at Chisha, enticed the chiefs of the Yi villages—some rose in answer to Chun—and advanced to attack Youyang county; the commandery quaked with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s Guo Chun crossed from Fuling, camped at Chisha, suborned tribal headmen, struck Youyang, and terrified the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 牧問朝吏曰：「西蜀傾覆，邊境見侵，何以禦之？

translations.literal: Mu asked court clerks, saying, "Western Shu has fallen and our border is invaded—how do we defend it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu asked his staff how to answer Wei’s probe.

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「今二縣山險，諸夷阻兵，不可以軍驚擾，驚擾則諸夷盤結。

translations.literal: " They all replied, "The two counties are rugged; the Yi hold the passes—you cannot shake them with troops or they will knot together in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: They urged patience: “The hills will explode if you march.”

sentences.zh: 宜以漸安，可遣恩信吏宣教慰勞。

translations.literal: It is fitting to pacify gradually; dispatch trusted officers to preach kindness and calm them."
translations.idiomatic: “Send envoys and soothe them bit by bit.”

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Mu said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Mu said, “No.”

sentences.zh: 外境內侵，誑誘人民，當及其根柢未深而撲取之，此救火貴速之勢也。

translations.literal: When a foreign power pushes inside and seduces your people, you strike while its roots are still shallow—that is the same urgency as putting out a fire.
translations.idiomatic: “Hit the infection before it spreads—firefighting rewards speed.”

sentences.zh: 」敕外趣嚴，掾史沮儀者便行軍法。

translations.literal: " He ordered full readiness outside; any clerk who blocked the plan faced military law.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered war footing and threatened mutinous staff with martial discipline.

sentences.zh: 撫夷將軍高尚說牧曰：「昔潘太常督兵五萬，然後以討五谿夷耳。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Yi Gao Shang urged Mu, saying, "Formerly Grand Master Pan led fifty thousand men before he could punish the five-streams Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang reminded him: “Pan Jun needed fifty thousand for these hills.”

sentences.zh: 是時劉氏連和，諸夷率化，今既無往日之援，而郭純已據遷陵，而明府以三千兵深入，尚未見其利也。

translations.literal: The Liu family was then allied with us and the tribes were mostly loyal; now that support is gone, Guo Chun already holds Qianling, yet you would push three thousand men deep—I do not yet see the gain."
translations.idiomatic: “Today there is no Shu buffer, Guo Chun sits on Qianling—three thousand men buys nothing.”

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「非常之事，何得循舊？

translations.literal: " Mu said, "In a crisis you do not copy old playbooks.
translations.idiomatic: Mu answered, “Emergencies break precedent.”

sentences.zh: 」即率所領，晨夜進道，緣山險行，垂二千里，從塞上，斬惡民懷異心者魁帥百餘人及其支黨凡於余級，純等散，五谿平。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his command, marching day and night along cliff tracks nearly two thousand li, came down from the heights, and beheaded more than a hundred ringleaders of wicked locals who harbored treason with their followers—over a thousand heads in all; Guo Chun’s force scattered and the five streams were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the passes, took a thousand heads, broke Guo Chun, and quieted the five streams.

sentences.zh: 遷公安督、揚武將軍，封都鄉侯，徙濡須督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervisor of Gong'an, promoted General Who Rouses Might, enfeoffed marquis of Duxiang, and moved to supervisor of Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to Ruxu command as General Who Rouses Might and marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧之在濡须，深以进取可图，而不敢陈其策，与侍中东观令硃育宴，慨然叹息。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: While Mu held Ruxu he believed the north could be attacked yet dared not speak his plan; feasting with Palace Attendant Zhu Yu, director of the Eastern Institute, he sighed again and again.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu says he burned to strike north but stayed silent at Ruxu, only sighing over wine with Zhu Yu.

sentences.zh: 育谓牧恨於策爵未副，因谓牧曰：「朝廷诸君，以际会坐取高官，亭侯功无与比，不肯在人下，见顾者犹以於邑，况於侯也！

translations.literal: Yu thought Mu resented that rewards had not matched his schemes and said, "Courtiers who lucked into high rank cannot stand your merit; even critics pity you—how much more you, a marquis!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu thought he brooded on rank and flattered him.

sentences.zh: 」牧笑而答曰：「卿之所言，未获我心也。

translations.literal: " Mu smiled and replied, "You have not read my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Mu smiled, “You miss my point.”

sentences.zh: 马援有言，人当功多而赏薄。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan said men should bear much merit and little reward.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan said the worthy deserve thin pay for heavy work.

sentences.zh: 吾功不足录，而见宠已过当，岂以为恨？

translations.literal: My deeds scarcely merit record, yet favor already exceeds what is due—why should I resent that?
translations.idiomatic: “My record is slight; the throne has already overpaid me—what grudge is there?”

sentences.zh: 国家不深相知，而见害朝人，是以默默不敢有所陈。

translations.literal: The throne does not know me well, while courtiers slander me—so I keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: “Court gossip pins me down, so I hold my tongue.”

sentences.zh: 若其不然，当建进取之计，以报所受之恩，不徒自守而已，愤叹以此也。

translations.literal: Were it otherwise I would lay plans to advance and repay grace—not merely dig in—and my sighs come from that."
translations.idiomatic: “If I were trusted I would attack, not just garrison—that is what grieves me.”

sentences.zh: 」育复曰：「国家已自知侯，以侯之才，无为不成。

translations.literal: " Yu said again, "The state knows you; with your talent nothing fails.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu pressed him to speak.

sentences.zh: 愚谓自可陈所怀。

translations.literal: In my foolish view you may state what you feel."
translations.idiomatic: “Say what you think.”

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「武安君谓秦王云：『非成业难，得贤难；

translations.literal: " Mu said, "Lord Wu'an told the King of Qin: 'Finishing a great work is not the hard part; finding the worthy is hard;'
translations.idiomatic: Mu quoted Lord Bai Qi: “Finishing the work is easy—finding talent is hard.”

sentences.zh: 非得贤难，用之难；

translations.literal: it is not finding the worthy that is hard; employing him is hard;'
translations.idiomatic: “Finding him is easy—using him is hard.”

sentences.zh: 非用之难，任之难。

translations.literal: it is not employing that is hard; trusting him is hard.'"
translations.idiomatic: “Using him is easy—trusting him is hard.”

sentences.zh: 』武安君欲为秦王并兼六国，恐授事而不见任，故先陈此言。

translations.literal: Lord Wu'an meant to swallow the six states for Qin yet feared being tasked without trust, so he spoke first.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi spoke first because he feared empty mandate.

sentences.zh: 秦王既许而不能，卒陨将成之业，赐剑杜邮。

translations.literal: The king promised yet could not deliver, ruined the campaign, and gave him the sword at Duyou.
translations.idiomatic: The king broke his word and killed Bai Qi at Duyou.

sentences.zh: 今国家知吾，不如秦王之知武安，而害吾者有过范睢。

translations.literal: The throne knows me less than Qin knew Bai Qi, and my slanderers outdo Fan Ju.
translations.idiomatic: “Wu trusts me less than Qin trusted Bai Qi, and my enviers surpass Fan Ju.”

sentences.zh: 大皇帝时，陆丞相讨鄱阳，以二千人授吾，潘太常讨武陵，吾又有三千人，而朝廷下议，弃吾於彼，使江渚诸督，不复发兵相继。

translations.literal: Under the Great Emperor Chancellor Lu attacked Poyang with two thousand men for me; Grand Master Pan took three thousand to Wuling—yet the court voted to abandon me and kept the river generals from sending relief.
translations.idiomatic: “Sun Quan gave me five thousand once, then court debate stranded me while river commands refused reinforcements.”

sentences.zh: 蒙国威灵自济，今日何为常。

translations.literal: I survived only by the state’s good fortune; why should today be different?
translations.idiomatic: “I saved myself by luck—why expect better now?”

sentences.zh: 向使吾不料时度宜，苟有所陈，至见委以事，不足兵势，终有败绩之患，何无不成之有？」〉

translations.literal: Had I misread the hour and rashly spoken, been given command without troops, I would have courted rout—how could anything succeed?"〉
translations.idiomatic: “Had I misjudged and begged for troops I lacked, I would have failed—silence was wisdom.”〉

sentences.zh: 復以前將軍假節，領武陵太守。

translations.literal: Again he served as General of the Front with lent credentials, leading Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as General of the Front with credential-axe over Wuling.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，士民思之。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus; gentry and commoners missed him.
translations.idiomatic: He left no hoard, yet people mourned him.

sentences.zh: 子褘嗣，代領兵。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited and took command of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongli Hui succeeded him in the army.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧次子盛，亦履恭让，为尚书郎。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: Mu's second son Sheng also practiced courtesy and yielding and was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Second son Sheng was a courteous gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弟徇领兵为将，拜偏将军，戍西陵，与监军使者唐盛论地形势，谓宜城、信陵为建平援，若不先城，敌将先入。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xun commanded troops as a general, was appointed General of the Side, garrisoned Xiling; with Supervising Army Envoy Tang Sheng he discussed terrain, arguing Yicheng and Xinling should shield Jianping—if not fortified first, the enemy would seize them first.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhongli Xun, a side general on the Xiling line, told Tang Sheng that Yicheng and Xinling must be walled for Jianping’s sake.

sentences.zh: 盛以施绩、留平，智略名将，屡经於彼，無云當城之者，不然徇计。

translations.literal: Sheng held that Shi Ji and Liu Ping, famed strategists who had often operated there, had never called for fortifying them, and he rejected Xun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Sheng cited Shi Ji and Liu Ping—veterans who had never demanded those walls—and brushed the plan aside.

sentences.zh: 后半年，晋果遣将脩信陵城。

translations.literal: Half a year later Jin indeed sent a general to build up Xinling.
translations.idiomatic: Six months on Jin fortified Xinling as Xun had warned.

sentences.zh: 晋军平吴，徇领水军督，临陈战死。〉

translations.literal: When Jin's army pacified Wu, Xun commanded the navy and died in battle facing the line.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Jin conquered Wu, Zhongli Xun led the river fleet and died in the fighting.〉

translations.literal: 【Evaluation】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：山越好為叛亂，難安易動，是以孫權不遑外御，卑詞魏氏。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The mountain Yue loved rebellion—they were hard to pacify and easy to stir—therefore Sun Quan had no leisure for outer defense and used humble words toward Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict: hill Yue were Wu’s chronic ulcer, which is why Sun Quan bowed low to Wei while sorting the interior.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸臣，皆克寧內難，綏靜邦域者也。

translations.literal: All these ministers were ones who could quell inner turmoil and quiet the realm.
translations.idiomatic: These men stamped out civil strife and steadied the state.

sentences.zh: 呂岱清恪在公；

translations.literal: Lü Dai was pure and scrupulous in public service;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai served with icy integrity;

sentences.zh: 周魴譎略多奇；

translations.literal: Zhou Fang’s stratagems were full of surprises;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang’s ruses were brilliant;

sentences.zh: 鐘離牧蹈長者之規；

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu trod the path of the elder gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu lived the old-school gentleman’s code;

sentences.zh: 全琮有當世之才，貴重於時，然不檢姦子，獲譏毀名云。

translations.literal: Quan Zong had talent for his age and was honored in his time, yet he failed to rein in wicked sons and earned blame that marred his name.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong was the age’s ablest yet lost his reputation by indulging corrupt sons.
